# Decisions D-250–D-499

Part of [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md), which lists every part. Entries keep their order; this part holds the numbers D-250–D-499.

<!-- entries -->
- **D-431 (2026-10-14, GitHub CI by manual dispatch only; user decision).** The `ci` workflow loses its `push` and
  `pull_request` triggers and keeps `workflow_dispatch` only (D-22's no-schedule rule is unchanged). Every run since
  2026-10-09 failed with jobs that never started (zero steps, no log), the signature of the private repository's
  Actions minutes or spending limit being exhausted (macOS legs count 10x, Windows 2x), and each failure emailed the user.
  The merge gate is the local full suite on the exact pushed commit through `tools/suite_queue.py` (D-400..D-409,
  D-427). The full cross-platform workflow is dispatched at the K.19.1 points (release tag, corpus deposit, thesis
  submission), with Actions billing checked first.
  - **Rejected:** keeping push CI with Linux only (still spends minutes on every push of a busy multi-session day);
    raising the spending limit (cost, while the local gate already covers every push); only muting the emails
    (failed runs keep accumulating and hide real CI results).
- **D-432 (2026-10-14, GUI design addendum; user request, approved as direction like D-390..D-399).** Three additions
  to `docs/reports/gui/design.md`: (1) Settings › Continuous integration offers three CI targets: local
  (`tools/ci_local.py`, the default), GitHub-hosted (dispatch, and the `CI_ON_PUSH` repository variable), and the Mac
  Studio as a self-hosted runner (`CI_RUNNER`); (2) every PROV-generating form has an on-by-default "W3C PROV conformance
  check" checkbox. Unticking it needs an acknowledged warning and maps to a proposed core option
  `--skip-prov-conformance` (G2c-5) that skips tier 4 only, marks the corpus unvalidated, and blocks sealing and release
  until `validate --corpus` passes; it is never allowed with `--release` or in the regeneration round; (3) Settings ›
  Compute exposes every compute setting: machine preset (`--m5ultra`, `--preset`), per-command `--jobs`, stagger, the
  queue's CPU and memory budgets, the test-gate worker count, and ingest limits read-only.
  - **Rejected:** a GUI-only skip that bypasses the CLI (breaks the CLI-only write rule); allowing the skip in release
    mode; editable ingest limits in the GUI (they are part of a corpus's recorded identity, so they stay profile edits).
  - **Amended 2026-10-15 (user decision):** `validate --corpus` stays read-only and does not clear the mark. Only a full
    `recompute --corpus OLD --out NEW --stages sem,prov,validation` produces an unmarked corpus, never in place. A
    derive never carries a skipped validation layer (`version_mismatch`). The GUI's "Revalidate (full recompute)…"
    action runs that recompute (design §8.3a, fe399912).
- **D-270 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: the DRIFT build behind the existing mapper; user-approved 2026-10-13).** The
  `drift.k18.*` variants are mapped by a new module `adapters/agentdojo/drift_mapper.py`, entered from
  `TraceLoggerMapper.map` by a dispatch on the variant, so the adapter id, the execution-id prefix and the AgentDyn
  profile stay as D.6.5 says. The dispatch in `mapper.py`/`dialect.py` is routed to the owner of those files
  (`docs/reports/phase10l/routing.md`).
  - **Rejected:** a separate mapper id `agentdojo.drift` (departs from D.6.5; AgentDyn part `c` would need a second
    profile); subclassing the private `_Build` (couples to code another session owns; DRIFT differs in nearly every
    step); hooks only (cannot change the structural reads).
- **D-271 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: a `drift` rule catalogue; user-approved 2026-10-13).** New rules go in
  `adapters/agentdojo/rules/drift.rules.toml` (namespace already homed in `aer/rules.py` and `citation.NAMESPACES`; D.5.4
  ids). The `agentdojo` catalogue gets no new entry; its generic rules are reused with their twins.
  - **Rejected:** `agentdojo.drift_*` entries (departs from D.5.4 ids).
- **D-272 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: evidence classes; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Every `drift.*` rule that reads DRIFT
  code is class D with an `_unverified` class-I twin; every DRIFT-format profile has `verified_code = []`
  (`code_identity` `range` for DRIFT head and history, `unpinned` elsewhere). All harness readings are therefore class I;
  logged values stay O.
  - **Rejected:** DRIFT head verified at `6fd3df47` (its runs predate that code state).
- **D-273 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: CALL ERROR as a validator denial; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Each CALL ERROR `user`
  message becomes a `decision` (actor the `drift` defence, verdict `deny`, subject the preceding assistant message,
  reason the content verbatim, `ext.drift.check` trajectory/checklist) and the message `generated_by` it, role kept.
  - **Rejected:** a part subject (the refused calls exist only as text); parsing the text first (D-277).
- **D-274 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: one isolation decision per tool output; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Per tool message:
  the `tool_execution`, a `decision` (verdict `other`, subtype `drift.isolation_pass`, subject the execution,
  `unk {"/original": "ambiguous", "/reason": "not_recorded"}`), and the message `generated_by` it (C.5.5). The SEM tool
  label for such messages is a routed change to `semantics/suites.py`; until it lands, DRIFT tool outputs get integrity
  `unknown` (fail closed).
  - **Refinement from the code (2026-10-13, implementation):** only the **last** tool message of each call batch gets the
    decision: `DRIFTLLM.query` runs the detector on `messages[-1]` and `injection_isolate` edits `messages[-1]` only. The
    data agree: excised injection frames occur only in last positions in every source (`docs/reports/phase10l/census.md`
    §5).
  - **Rejected:** `redact`/`modify` on every output (asserts edits that mostly did not happen); a frame-based `redact`
    heuristic (SEM's, regeneration-batch item 6); `content_state` only (leaves a possibly edited output attributed to
    the environment alone).
- **D-275 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: what DRIFT does not log stays unknown; user-approved 2026-10-13).** The agent's model
  call has `unk /input not_recorded`; DRIFT's own LLM calls get no records; `ext.drift.text_form` states re-serialised
  or raw text.
  - **Rejected:** placeholder model calls per sub-call kind (would invent counts and order).
- **D-276 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: plan-field semantics per part, checked per file; user-approved 2026-10-13).** The
  profile declares `initial_plan` or `final_plan_state`; the mapper writes `ext.drift.plan_semantics` and raises
  `drift.plan_semantics_contradicted` (writing no semantics) where raw planner text appears under `final_plan_state`.
  One-directional: the data cannot refute `initial_plan`.
- **D-277 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: proposed calls not executed; user-approved 2026-10-13).** No re-parsing in v0.1;
  final turns with call text and no `tool_calls` raise `drift.calls_in_text_not_executed` (detail `reserialised` or
  `raw`); partial drops are a datasheet limitation.
- **D-278 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: identity, benchmark label, outcomes; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Model from the
  directory (= `pipeline_name`, the requested model) or the AgentDyn table; the `drift` defence from the key set;
  `benchmark_version` is `suite_version` for AgentDojo suites and `label_not_suite_version` for AgentDyn suites
  (departs from the D.4.4 sketch); benign `security` is `harness_default` under `drift.benign_security_constant@1`.
- **D-279 (2026-10-13, phase 10l: sources, parts, the history set; user-approved 2026-10-13).** New registration `drift`
  with parts `head` (1,569) and `history` (1,046 at `53dbc6c5`, licence policy `reference`: committed and deleted before
  any licence statement; fetched with the user's approval, R-1, 13.2 MB); AgentDyn `d` stays `owned_elsewhere`; AgentDyn
  `c`, EnvironmentOptim and drift-1 DRIFT parts are mapped through their owners' profiles. Open: EnvironmentOptim's 620
  (probably AgentDyn history, unchecked); drift-1's 10 PACT files are mapped generically with their extra keys.
  - **Addendum (user decisions 2026-10-13): Figshare 32657856's DRIFT part is excluded; the general criterion was
    withdrawn.** The user first excluded Figshare's DRIFT part from the systematic process because no attack succeeded
    (0 of 2,847 attacked runs; the deposit's `v1.k14` runs are not covered: 772 of 12,337 attacked runs succeed), then
    generalised the rule to every source at arm/part level, then, asked again through the orchestrator because it selects
    on the outcome, **withdrew the generalisation ("Figshare DRIFT only", reconfirmed 2026-10-13)**. Only the Figshare
    ruling stood at that point. **Reversed by the user later on 2026-10-13 ("yes undo the figshare DRIFT"; confirmed in
    the orchestrator session): Figshare's 2,847 DRIFT runs are included like every other part, and data with no
    successful attacks is never excluded.** Phase 10j registers that part for mapping by the DRIFT build. The AgentDyn C DRIFT arms
    `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07-drift` and `gpt-5.1-2025-11-13-drift` (0 successes each) and drift-1's PACT arm stay in.
    - **Record of the measurement** (phase-10c census, 26 sources, 351,223 attacked runs, 749 arms by layout prefix and
      pipeline directory): the withdrawn rule would have removed 242 arms with 34,074 attacked runs, mostly defence arms
      that blocked every attack (gate on, MELON, Kavach, Glitch, Interbolt, the Zenodo capability caps); at source level
      only Kavach `main` and yockcheng. Figshare's 165 visible injection frames all sit in non-last batch positions,
      which DRIFT's isolation never inspects, consistent with the defence working; the datasheet states the 0-of-2,847
      count and this observation as context (no exclusion).
- **D-290 (2026-10-13, phase 9b: a poisoned capture log quarantines its session; user-approved 2026-10-13).** When T0 ingests a staged
  session whose capture log holds the constant `error` event of a failed redaction scan (`where: "capture.redact"`,
  C.13.10 item 6), it quarantines the session exactly as a literal-secret hit does (`capture.quarantined`, nothing
  stored, staging kept, the attempt counts and is not re-attempted), whatever T0's own literal scan finds. The poisoned
  log itself holds no content of the failed event, but the files beside it are not written through the redactor: in the
  end-to-end test the benchmark's native temporary log holds the very value the scan failed on. Before this, such a
  session was quarantined only when T0's literal scan happened to hit one of those files, and otherwise stored as an
  errored execution. Detail text names the reason; register code unchanged.
  - **Rejected:** storing the poisoned log as an errored execution (the C.13.10 reading "the session ends `errored`"
    taken alone): content-free as a log, but it would admit its unredacted siblings whenever the literal scan misses
    (a value T0 does not hold, a spelling the scan does not cover); a new register code (`capture.redaction_failed`)
    (a `corpus/` change for no extra information: the detail says which reason applied).
- **D-291 (2026-10-13, phase 9b: the A9 preflight is decided from the reply; user-approved 2026-10-13).** `run_probe` no longer reads
  "roles accepted" from a 2xx status. `runner.roles_verdict` reads the recorded (redacted) response body of the last
  reply: `accepted` only when the reply follows the instruction that only the system message carries (call
  `get_probe_value` with the key `q7f3-probe`, structured or as text); `refused` on a non-2xx status, a 2xx body with an
  `error` object, or a role refusal in its text; `unconfirmed` for a 2xx that shows neither (the roles may be ignored
  silently; also no choices, `finish_reason: error`, a non-JSON body); `unknown` without a reply. The results carry
  `roles` and `roles_reason`; `roles_accepted` is `roles == "accepted"`. T0 refuses `refused` and `unconfirmed` (exit 4,
  `cli.refused.preflight`, the reason in the message). The probe key changed from `a` (guessable) to a distinctive
  value, so the instrumentation item is now `agentdojo.preflight_probe@2`. Headers never enter the verdict; the
  `wire_headers` note keeps allowlisted values only (tested with cookie, key and organisation headers). Probe sessions
  are never stored, so no corpus byte moves.
  - **Rejected:** keeping 2xx as acceptance (a gateway that answers 200 with `{"error": ...}` or drops the developer
    message passes A9); an opt-in flag to run with `unconfirmed` roles (no use case yet; a model that cannot follow a
    one-line system instruction fails A4/A9 in practice anyway).
- **D-292 (2026-10-13, phase 9b: the executor guard is keyed by interpreter; user-approved 2026-10-13).** `ast.dump` output differs
  between Python minor versions, so `executor_mirror` keeps the AST digest of the mirrored `ToolsExecutor.query` per
  interpreter (`cpython-3.12` only, the backend interpreter). On an interpreter without a recorded digest `guard()`
  raises the typed `MirrorUnverifiable` (a `MirrorMismatch`, code `backend.mirror.interpreter`) before comparing, so the
  cell is refused with the true reason instead of a false "method differs". A digest for another interpreter is added
  only after the mirror's differential test passes on it. No capture or AER byte changes on 3.12.
  - **Rejected:** comparing the source digest instead (formatting-sensitive; the fork is AST-identical, not
    source-identical, verify/autodojo.md #18); computing digests for 3.13/3.14 now (untested there).
- **D-293 (2026-10-13, phase 9b: live ledger `index_status`; user-approved 2026-10-13).** The ledger entry's `index_status` is the
  status of the execution's index row. `LiveSessionPipeline.ingest` returned `None` because the corpus writer queues rows
  until a flush. Phase 9b first worked around it in the campaign (a flush before reading the row); the root cause was then
  fixed in `adapters/runner/session.py` by the deferrals session (R-9b-3: `CorpusWriter.pending_row`), so the campaign
  takes `SessionOutcome.status` as is and the workaround is retired. The tests assert the ledger entry equals the row in
  `executions.jsonl` after the flush. Only the `live.sessions` block of a live working manifest changes (no live corpus
  exists outside tests); no AER, SEM or PROV byte moves.
  - **Rejected:** leaving `null` (the manifest field promised by H.2.2 `LiveBlock` was never filled).
- **D-310 (2026-10-13, routed item R-10k-2: key cuts in the release scan; user-approved 2026-10-13).** gitleaks cuts a
  match at its fragment boundaries on long lines (a fragment is about 100 kB plus up to 25 kB of look-ahead), so on the
  full-size credleak PROV files 5 `apv:derivationKey` matches were cut beyond the 2026-10-12 allowlist (field names to
  3-5 characters, one key to 12) and reported as `generic-api-key`. Measured on gitleaks 8.30.1 with synthetic lines:
  `StartColumn` and `EndColumn` count from the fragment start, not the line (a cut at byte 125,000 of a line is
  reported as column 1), so a match cannot be located by its columns; `EndColumn - StartColumn + 1` is the match's byte
  length (301 of 301 findings, also with CRLF line ends and multibyte text), and `Entropy` is the Shannon entropy of the
  secret. Ruling:
  - **The allowlist hides uncut members only:** `^(derivationKey":"|subject_key":"ex_|logical_key":"lk_)[a-z2-7]{26}"$`
    (each field with its own prefix). The cut alternatives of 2026-10-12 are removed: a 6-character suffix such as
    `ionKey`, `ct_key` or `al_key` also ends `sessionKey`, `project_key` or `local_key`, so a real 16-26 character
    lower-case base32 value under such a name, cut there, was hidden. The configuration digest changes.
  - **A key-cut check in `tools/release_scan.py`** (`key_cut_explained`, check version 1) resolves cuts against the
    file. For a `generic-api-key` finding on one line with `Secret == "REDACTED"` and one `REDACTED` in `Match`, the
    redacted match gives the text before and after the value, and the length gives the value's length. Every position
    on the line where that text and a value of that length fit must lie inside an exact member (`[{,]` then
    `"apv:derivationKey":"<26>"`, `"subject_key":"ex_<26>"` or `"logical_key":"lk_<26>"`, then `[,}]`), and at least one
    must give a value with the reported entropy. Anything else (another position fits, the line cannot be read or is
    longer than 64 MiB, a member is missing) keeps the finding. A real `apiKey` cut to `Key":"` on a line of
    derivation keys therefore stays a finding, and so does the derivation-key cut beside it (the ambiguity is reported).
  - **Values:** the redacted `Match` and the line are held in memory only; `Line` is never read. The scan document still
    records path, rule, line and fingerprint per finding; the gitleaks tool entry gains `key_cuts_resolved` (a count,
    never which findings) and its `mode` names the check version. The builder reads neither.
  - **Why:** the routed per-fingerprint triage (option b) would recur on every large corpus; resolving the cut against
    the file's own bytes is stricter than any match-text pattern, because the decision rests on the whole member.
  - **Rejected:** lowering `_MIN_FIELD_SUFFIX` to 3 (`Key":"` hides `apiKey":"<26 base32>"`); locating the match by
    `StartColumn` (fragment-relative); re-implementing gitleaks' fragmentation to recover offsets (version-specific);
    masking keys and re-running gitleaks over a copy (writes corpus text to disk and scans a different tree); a second
    gitleaks run on the flagged line through stdin (its fragments differ, so a real secret can be cut out of it).
  - **Downstream:** `tools/` and its tests only. No AER, SEM, PROV, corpus or manifest bytes change; nothing is
    regenerated. Release scans written from now on carry the new configuration digest, mode and count; existing scan
    documents stay valid for their root digests. **Measured** on the phase-10k C3 scratch tree (released AER/SEM/PROV of
    14,214 runs, 2.0 GB; read-only, 564 s): 18 key cuts resolved (the 5 of R-10k-2 and 13 that the old cut-suffix
    allowlist hid), no `generic-api-key` finding left in PROV; the 8 AER and 1 `curl-auth-user` fingerprints are
    unchanged (14 → 9 fingerprints; with C2's raw object, about 10 for triage).
- **D-360 (2026-10-13, fixture-tree caps; user decision in the orchestrator session, implemented on branch `fixture-cap`).**
  The fixture tree's total cap rises from 8 MiB to **16 MiB**, and each **source** (a top-level directory of
  `tests/fixtures/`) gets a budget of **512 KiB**, larger only with a recorded reason. The caps live in
  `tests/FIXTURES.json` (`agentprov-fixture-caps/0.1`): `caps` (total, per file 1 MiB, per source), `oversize_files`
  (path and reason; the two complete `.eval` logs) and `source_exceptions` (source, `budget_bytes`, reason). Existing
  exceptions on 2026-10-13: `inspect` 3,049,864 B, `agentdojo_prov_v1` 1,071,984 B, `openhands` 1,025,419 B, `capture`
  566,153 B, each with a budget rounded up to the next 64 KiB. One checker, `agentprov.testing.fixture_caps`, is used by
  `tests/golden/test_golden_index.py` and `tests/repo/test_fixture_caps.py`; stale or unreasoned entries fail too. Spec
  K.4.1(5).
  - **Why:** several new families arrived in parallel and the 8 MiB tree held 7.59 MB; a per-source budget keeps any one
    source from taking the headroom, and a reason makes every exception reviewable.
  - **Where the file lives:** beside the tree, not in it: `.claude/settings.json` closes `tests/fixtures/**` to agents'
    reads (K.4.1(4), R-42), and the caps are policy, not fixture content, so agents must be able to read and edit them.
  - **Rejected:** keeping the caps as constants in a test (the reasons would be spread over test files); a budget per
    file only (one source could still fill the tree).
- **D-260 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: the credential-leak family, unit and selection; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Zenodo
  22737462 v3 (rank 5 of D-145, CC-BY-4.0) gets a new family `credleak` with dialect and mapper `credleak.cell`, variant
  `v1` (the census proposed `p15b-v3`; as for dtap, the variant numbers the record shape and the profile pins the deposit
  version). One execution per `runs[]` entry (19,636 in 643 cell members; the phase-10e card's 654 counted other JSON),
  primary locator `{"p": "/runs/<i>"}` into the cell member (HL H.7.1). The profile selects the cells under
  `01-injection-map/`, `03-egress-axis/` and `04-hygiene/`; every other member is `select.not_execution_artefact`. The
  layout class (roster, `excluded-models`, underscore directories) and the file prefix are observed path facets in
  `ext.credleak`, never identity. Rate exclusions go in `rates.toml`, not into the import. Runs without tool calls stay.
  Spec: D.19; census: `docs/reports/phase10k/census.md`.
  - **Rejected:** importing only the roster (drops 2,362 runs the deposit keeps on purpose); one execution per cell
    (merges up to 160 runs).
- **D-261 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: identity; user-approved 2026-10-13).** `agent.model.requested` is the run's `model`
  string verbatim (O; routing prefixes kept); served model, provider and parameters are `not_recorded`. The harness is
  not named by any run file: `unk /instrumentation not_recorded`. `config` is kept verbatim in `ext.credleak`;
  `config.judgeModel` produced nothing (`intentVerdicts` all null) and gets no actor.
  - **Rejected:** mapping labels to vendor model ids (invention); a judge actor from `judgeModel`.
- **D-262 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: turns, calls and pairing; user-approved 2026-10-13, with Q1 answered "no model
  calls").** Per turn: a `user` message; per `toolCalls[]` entry an assistant message with one `tool_call` part (actor and
  role I), a `tool_execution` (I, no harness code verified) whose `call` is that part, and a `tool` result message
  whose `responds_to` is the call of the same entry (D, `credleak.pair_same_entry@1`: record structure, not order); then
  the turn's `assistantResponse` as an agent message ordered after the user message only (an empty text is `parts: []`).
  No `model_call` is written: boundaries are not recorded and `maxTurns` = 10 allows several calls per turn, so agent
  messages declare `generated_by` `not_recorded` and the seal carries `missing_generated_by`. Tool names and inputs are
  verbatim, malformed ones included; `credleak.tools@1` lists the 10 canonical names and reads every other name as
  `unknown`.
  - **Rejected:** one `model_call` per turn at class I (it would be false for multi-call turns); edges from the
    assistant text to the tool results (its position is not recorded).
- **D-263 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: time; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Turn timestamps are kept verbatim in
  `ext.credleak` and the turn scope's `/t` is `ambiguous` (`credleak.turn_timestamp_role@1`): start and end cannot be
  told apart (in 9,505 of 18,993 consecutive run pairs the next run starts before the previous run's duration has
  elapsed). Durations, the cell `timestamp` and `runId` are ext only. No typed time is written (the dtap precedent,
  D.16.4 correction 1).
- **D-264 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: harness signals; user-approved 2026-10-13).** The run-level detector fields become
  `judgement` records, value O verbatim, `/t` and `/inputs` not recorded. As built (D.19.6) the actor is `det` (kind
  judge, role `detector`, I) with origin `checker` (I), refining the census wording (actor `harness`, origin
  `harness_default`). No polarity is read: the deposit corrected one flag after the runs. `canaryDetected`,
  `canaryInInput` and `canaryInOutput` are kept as booleans and `canariesFound[]` as a count only.
  - **Rejected:** copying the `canariesFound` labels (they embed the tag and would force escalation).
- **D-265 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: the withholding policy of profile `credleak-p15b`; user-approved 2026-10-13, Q2
  "object scope", Q4 "lower-case prose stays outside").** The first shipped `[withhold]` table (D-234): `reason =
  "secret"` (D-146), a one-line `public_note`, `scan_rules`, and four rules, all scope `object`: `canary-tag` (pattern
  `CANARY[^_]`), `canary-tag-left` (pattern `[^_/]CANARY`), `aws-key-shape` (`AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`) and `sk-key-shape`
  (`sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,256}`). The census proposed the bare marker; the part-C2 seal showed it also matches two
  not-selected collector-log labels in the released `raw/members.jsonl` (a `chain` failure), and the C1 re-run found one
  run holding the tag only in the left-bounded form. Expected on the full import: 325 cells, the collector-log JSON and
  the deposit zip withheld; 5,422 executions withheld by derived-hit escalation (D-235); 14,214 released, 4,415 of them
  with their raw object withheld. C1 matched the census set exactly (0 mismatches).
  - **Rejected:** scope `executions` (releases 9,799, dropping 4,415 runs that hold no value); masking in the mapper
    (aer/0.1 cannot express it); withholding nothing (D-146).
- **D-266 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: fixtures; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Fixtures are whole, unedited clean cell members
  (11 cells, 124 runs) chosen by criterion among the 318 clean cells, with attribution in `SOURCE.json` and
  `tests/fixtures/LICENSES/`. `tools/credleak/build_fixtures.py` re-checks every chosen member against the profile's
  `[withhold]` rules and refuses any hit.
- **D-267 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: the end-to-end withholding test; user-approved 2026-10-13).**
  `tests/adapters/credleak/test_withhold_e2e.py` replaces the injection at `corpus.withhold.policy_of_profile` with the
  shipped profile: a deposit zip assembled at test time (clean fixtures plus cells carrying test-made sentinels
  assembled at run time, never committed) → import → release seal → `verify --level chain --release` → gitleaks release
  scan (with a sidecar control) → deposit build, nothing monkeypatched. Test names and messages carry rule ids only.
- **D-268 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: versions; user-approved 2026-10-13, download approved in chat).** Only v3 is pinned
  and imported. v1 and v2 were read in memory only and compared by run content digest: no run is missing from v3 (v1's
  one other run is the unredacted form of a run v3 holds redacted). v1 is never stored in a raw store (it holds an
  unredacted account identifier).
- **D-269 (2026-10-13, phase 10k: triage of the credleak release-scan findings; user decision 2026-10-13).** The findings
  the part-C3 full-size estimate predicts after D-310 (about 10; `docs/reports/phase10k/trials.md` §C3) are

- **D-320 (2026-10-13, R-10k-1: multi-execution whole-file artefacts in the runner; the runner edit and the empty-cell
  and collapse-subject choices user-approved 2026-10-13; first drafted as D-269 and renumbered, with the user's yes, into

  records and seal, as container mode does (`split_unit_frames`). The importer resumes (`skipped_resume`) and collapses
  across snapshots (H.7.2, D-202) each execution by its **source key**, after mapping (`known_keys`; `_seen_before(key=)`),
  and `--limit` counts each execution. The `dedup.collapsed` subject of such an execution is `{source_key}` (H.6.2), one
  entry per run. Strict-loader failures and crashed or limited jobs stay one degenerate AER per file, keyed by
  `{"p": ""}`; a file whose document-root key is indexed is resumed whole before mapping, never re-mapped into items
  (the same evidence twice; required by the deferrals session's review, which approved the design). A cell of the dialect with no run is `select.not_execution_artefact` with no AER (invariant 2). Readers
  without the attribute keep the digest key, the path-subject collapse entry and exactly their frames and job
  parameters; `map_artefact_total` keeps the single-item rule for every reader. D.2.9 note item 12; D.19.14.

    paused before the merge is refused on resume (G4). The `credleak` adapter code digest moves (no corpus).

    assert a run the file does not hold); the per-cell `{snapshot_id, path}` collapse subject (the two runs of a cell
    would share one `rid`, so the register could not say which runs collapsed).

    re-derive carries them.

- **D-311 (2026-10-13, RW-1: a `[withhold]` rule that selects executions by an AER seal issue code; trigger chosen by the
  user 2026-10-13 together with D-289 (c)).** A `[[withhold.rules]]` entry may carry `issue = "<namespace>.<code>"`
  instead of `marker` or `pattern` (exactly one of the three; no `scope` key, the rule withholds executions; optional
  per-rule `reason` and `public_note` as before; one rule per code). At sealing, every execution whose index row lists
  `map.<namespace>.<code>` or that has a register entry with that code is withheld with its primary object, exactly as
  a derived-file hit is (D-234). The other executions that cite that object stay released, and `chain` counts the object
  as `raw_withheld` for them (D-235). Basis `profile_rule`; finding `{agentprov-withhold/1, <profile>@<v>:<rule id>,
  <AER path>:<rule id>}`; the code and any value stay out of `WITHHELD.json`. Marker and pattern rules are unchanged and
  stay the byte-level backstop, scanned exactly as before (an issue rule is never matched against bytes).
  `corpus/` names no family: the code is data in the profile, evaluated against index rows and the register. First user:
  MCPHunt (phase 10m), whose mapper emits `mcphunt.canary_flagged` for every trace with a canary-flagged event (agreed
  with phase 10m through the orchestrator; profile entry `{id = "canary-flagged", issue = "mcphunt.canary_flagged"}`).
  - **Why:** D-289 (c): the source records which traces expose a planted canary (4,595 flagged), and 2,191 unflagged
    traces stay releasable although a raw file holds up to 723 traces. The flag lives in three released places (the AER
    seal, the index row, the register), and the register survives withholding (D-231), so the selection can be
    re-derived offline (D-314). An issue code is declared in a closed, versioned list (the catalogue's `issue_codes`,
    AD-18), so an unknown code can be refused when the policy is read (D-313).
  - **Rejected:** a rule over a recorded AER field (the 10m README's wording): the field (per-event `ext` flags) is
    declared nowhere, so parsing can check its syntax but not its existence, a mapper change could silently change the
    selection, `corpus/` would need a pointer-and-predicate language over AER records, and after the seal the flag sits
    only in the withheld AERs in the private sidecar, so `chain` could not check that a withheld execution really
    matched; a table-level list of codes (`[withhold] issue_codes = [...]`, the orchestrator's first sketch): no rule id
    for the ledger's findings and no per-rule reason or note; withholding every execution that cites the object (the
    raw-hit `executions` scope): it would drop the 2,191 unflagged traces, the point of (c).
- **D-312 (2026-10-13, RW-1: `agentprov-withheld/0.2`; part of the design the user chose with D-311).** The frozen
  `withheld-0.1` schema (D-163) lists rule kinds as `marker | pattern`, so a ledger that records an issue rule needs a
  new version. `agentprov-withheld/0.2` is `/0.1` with `issue` added to `policies[].rules[].kind`; nothing else differs
  (`$id`, title and format constant aside). The version is a function of the content: a document is `/0.2` exactly when a
  policy has an issue rule, the reader refuses either version that disagrees, and a sealed corpus holds the schema copy
  of its version (`schemas/withheld-0.2.schema.json`, new in `SCHEMA_FILES` and `CORPUS_LAYER_FORMATS`). The `/0.1`
  schema file still regenerates byte for byte from the code.
  - **No existing corpus byte changes:** sealing one working corpus with origin/main's code and with this build gives
    identical trees and sidecars, without a policy (35 files) and with a pattern-only policy (40 files, `WITHHELD.json`
    included). No AER, SEM, PROV or validation digest moves (sealing only); `recompute --check` is unaffected; shipped
    `[withhold]` profiles (credleak-p15b on phase-10k-credleak: marker and pattern rules only) seal as before.
  - **Rejected:** editing the `/0.1` schema in place (D-163); writing `/0.2` for every ledger (it would move the bytes of
    every corpus that withholds, with no new information); leaving issue rules out of `policies` (the ledger would no
    longer name the policy applied, D-230).
- **D-313 (2026-10-13, RW-1: the issue code is checked against the catalogues the corpus records; layering).**
  `parse_policy` checks an issue rule's form (`<namespace>.<code>`, at most 128 characters) and, when given a lookup,
  that the code is declared. Sealing, `chain` and the deposit builder read the policy through `load_policy`: the
  profile's policy, then `check_issue_codes` against `declared_issue_codes(catalogues)`, where `catalogues` are the
  namespace versions the corpus records (`derivation.json` at sealing, `rule_catalogues` of a sealed manifest). The
  lookup reads the catalogue as package data through `agentprov.aer.rules.load_catalogue` (AD-14), which never imports
  an adapter family (D.2.1). `corpus/` already does the same in `package.py`, `derive.py` and `authority.py`, so
  `corpus/` does not import `adapters/` (M.5.2(1)). An unknown code, a namespace the corpus does not use or an unshipped
  version refuses the seal (`corpus.withhold.policy`, exit 4), fails `chain` (`withheld.policy_invalid`) and refuses the
  deposit (`release.refused.withhold_policy`).
  - **Rejected:** injecting a lookup from the CLI, as `derive.py` gets `Catalogues`: that injection exists for source
    and semantics profiles, which go through the adapter registry; catalogue reads already sit in `corpus/`, and threading a
    callable through `seal`, `verify` and `build_deposit` would add a way to skip the check; validating the code in
    `adapters/profiles.py` at load time: the loader does not validate `[withhold]` (D-234), and `chain` and the builder
    read the digest-checked profile copy under `rules/`, not through the loader; a structural check only: a misspelt
    code would silently select nothing and release every flagged execution.
- **D-314 (2026-10-13, RW-1: the backstops re-check issue rules offline).** `chain` (`withheld.issue_released`, failed):
  no released execution carries an issue rule's code in its index row, in a register entry, or in its AER seal (read in
  the per-execution pass). `chain` (`withheld.issue_unsupported`, failed): a `WITHHELD.json` finding that names an issue
  rule points at the AER path of an execution the register records with the code. The deposit builder
  (`release.refused.withhold_issue`, exit 4) repeats the first check from the register and the index; it parses no AER.
  Sealing runs `chain` in release mode, so a seal that missed a flagged execution fails before it is swapped in.
  - **What cannot be checked, and why:** that every withheld execution was withheld *for* the code. An object entry
    records one finding, and the other withheld executions' AERs are in the private sidecar. Over-withholding releases
    nothing, so it is not a leak; the forward check (nothing flagged is released) is complete.
  - **Rejected:** trusting `WITHHELD.json.policies` (D-236's reason holds); re-deriving the selection from the AER seals
    alone (withheld AERs leave the tree; the register is the released record that survives).

- **D-380 (2026-10-13, ingest-formats-3: container members of archive inputs; R-10p-6; user-approved 2026-10-13 with
  the deferrals session's review changes).** D-200's exit-5 refusal of an archive input of a container dialect is
  lifted. The archive input is expanded (D-200/D-249). Each selected container member (an Inspect `.eval`) is a
  candidate under its **chain label**: its member labels from the input down, joined with `!/`. It goes to
  `map_containers`, never `map_whole_files`. There it is expanded at its **absolute level** (`ContainerSpec.depth`: the
  level of its parent plus one, so a `.eval` directly in a split zip opens at 2), under its chain's depth allowance
  (`max_depth`, D-382), and mapped as from a tree. Profile globs (the reader's include, exclude, context and blob globs)
  are matched against each member's own label, the label `expand` matched at its level. The chain label is a register
  key only. Such a profile must declare `[import] include`. An `.eval`'s own expansion depends only on the reader's member
  patterns, so its member rows, objects and AERs are the same from a tree, a split zip, a nested zip or a `tar.zst`
  (differential test). Review changes, all built:
  - `derivation.json` stage maps are keyed by `(stage, fn_digest)` for `expand` (`corpus/stages.py`) in the importer
    (G4 check, document merge), `corpus/derive.py` (`_stages_of`, the H.8.4 stage comparison as sets of declared
    identities) and `corpus/verify.py`. One import records one `expand` entry per expansion function. G4 refuses a
    recorded selection under another expand function. A resume with another nested selection is refused (its profile
    changed). `package._stage` is never called with `expand` and is unchanged.
  - Candidates are routed per container dialect, asserted in the tests.
  - One subject rule: `ContainerSpec.prefixed` gives every member of an archive input the subject
    `<input>!/<chain>!/<member>`. No archive-input corpus is stored, so this moves no register byte.
  - A re-map (`recompute`, `verify --level rederive`) refuses an archive selection that the source's `derivation.json`
    does not record (`IdentityRefusedError`, exit 4). It compares selections, not profile digests: a re-map after a
    profile change that keeps the selection is the regeneration round's case (41d7a2f).
  - Carved blobs (D-218) are unchanged: a container unit's carve sources are the members of its `.eval`.
  - **Rejected:**
    - the reader's default include for archive inputs (it would need an adapter accessor);
    - matching profile globs against chain labels (a nested member would need profile globs that know the archive
      structure);
    - a separate archive-of-containers job kind (the container path already exists).
- **D-381 (2026-10-13: an inner archive is stored as its own member object; the user's choice (a) of
  `nested-design.md` §2).** A declared nested archive (D-382) is a selected member of its parent, stored with a `member`
  origin and expanded from the store like any level-2 container. Each level is then a stored, content-addressed object,
  so `recompute`, `rederive`, `verify --level chain`, withholding and purge need no new case. The cost is the inner
  archives' bytes in the raw store (control-arena: 3.86 GB). A `raw_policy = include` release ships them (a later
  decision may mark them re-derivable and not deposited).
  - **Rejected:**
    - (b) a seekable inflate view over the parent member with `zlib` checkpoints. It was prototyped on the real 2.09 GB
      member (61 MiB, 1 s to index), but it needs a nested descriptor, an origin kind and changes to `verify` and
      `withhold`, and a `tar.zst` parent cannot use it;
    - (c) a depth allowance only (5 samples).
- **D-382 (2026-10-13: `[import] nested`).** A key of the closed `[import]` table: `[[import.nested]]` entries
  `{id, pattern, under?, note?}` plus raises. Only `max_member_bytes` and `max_ratio` (the nested archive's own member
  gate) and `max_depth` (the deepest level opened at or below it) can be raised. Each raise must be at least the global
  default and at most a fixed constant in `ingest/limits.py`: `NESTED_MAX_DEPTH` 3, `NESTED_MAX_MEMBER_BYTES` 2 GiB,
  `NESTED_MAX_RATIO` 1,000. They are validated at profile load (`nested_raises`, `raw.members.nested_selection`):
  closed keys, unique ids, `under` chains without cycles, F-08 patterns, and each entry's level within its chain's
  allowance. The raises are not `IngestLimits` fields. They travel in `Selection.children`, so `limits_sha256` and
  `corpus.json` `limits` are unchanged. `selection_sha256` gains `children` only when there are any, so every existing
  digest is unchanged. A child's pattern takes precedence over `include`. A tar holds a selected member whole (D-57),
  so a size raise is not honoured under a tar parent (`ingest.archive.size`). `[import] nested` in a profile whose input
  is not an archive is refused at import (exit 5). It stays disjoint from D-323's `[import] limits` allowlist.
  - **Rejected:**
    - raising the global `max_member_bytes` or `max_archive_depth` (the brief: the global limits never change);
    - a load-time check that an include and a nested pattern overlap (glob intersection is not decidable in general;
      precedence is defined instead).
- **D-383 (2026-10-13: streamed nested members, commit on verify).** A selected nested archive above the global
  `max_member_bytes` is streamed. The header carries `"streamed": true`, `DATA` frames follow as `zipfile` inflates it,
  and the closing JSON frame is `{"end": {"index"}}` (the CRC-32 and byte count checked) or
  `{"abort": {"index", "code", "reason"}}`. The parent publishes it only after an `end` and its own size and CRC-32
  check in `put_chunks`. After an `abort` the spool is discarded and the member is rejected with the code. Any other
  sequence is `expand.protocol`. The job's member cap is the largest raise of its selection. Spools go to the store's
  `tmp_dir` (`WorkerPool(spool_dir=)`) as unnamed files, so a crash leaves none; a stale named temporary of a dead
  process is swept when the store opens. Members at or below the global bound keep D-58's read-whole path.
- **D-384 (2026-10-13: labels, origins and subjects at every level).** Member names stay labels (`logical_name`). The
  origin chain is `hf`/`zenodo` part → `split` descriptor → `member` (nested zip) → `member` (`.eval`) → `member`
  (sample). Every link is a stored object and no origin kind is added. A label containing `!/` is rejected
  `ingest.name.invalid` in a container at level 2 or below, and when it matches a nested pattern (level-1 members
  without declared nested archives are unchanged). `ExpandOutcome.placed` gives each container's chain, level and
  allowance, and `nested_members` the expanded archives, which are never candidates.
- **D-385 (2026-10-13: duplicates).** Byte duplicates collapse on the object digest: in one snapshot the later
  candidate in chain-label byte order gets `dedup.collapsed`, and across snapshots D-202 applies. Both origins are
  recorded, and the AER bytes do not depend on which copy came first. A truncated direct `.eval` and its complete nested
  copy are different bytes. The truncated one is `not_imported` (`ingest.archive.format`), the nested one is imported,
  and no relation is recorded or inferred from their shared name (invariant 2).
- **D-386 (2026-10-13: calibration and tests).** Calibration: `docs/reports/ingest-formats/nested-calibration.md`.
  Tests: `tests/adapters/runner/test_nested_archives.py` and `tests/unit/raw/test_nested_expand.py`, with synthetic
  archives built at test time. Regen-batch entry `ingest-formats-3`.
- **D-387 (2026-10-13: interactions).** The D-323 and D-382 key sets are disjoint, and a nested raise never reaches a
  leaf member. Carving (D-218) and multi-execution files (D-320) are unchanged, because they work on stored members. The
  merge waits until the runner session's D-321/D-323 are in; then this branch is rebased, and the deferrals session
  reviews the runner and importer diff.
- D-388–D-389 are reserved.
- **D-390..D-399 (2026-10-14, desktop GUI research, branch `gui-research`):** the direction for an AgentPROV desktop GUI. The evidence and measurements are in `docs/reports/gui/research.md`, the specification in `docs/reports/gui/design.md` and the wireframes in `docs/reports/gui/wireframes/`. The user approved the design as the direction; nothing is built yet. The open items are decided at build time: signing identities, the job and cache directory location, the scope of a Textual SSH companion, and an owner for the four small core changes (D-393, D-394, D-395, D-397).
- **D-390 (2026-10-14, GUI toolkit; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).** The GUI uses **PySide6 6.12 / Qt 6.12, Qt Widgets only**, from the `PySide6-Essentials` wheel.
  - **Licence:** LGPLv3, met by dynamic linking (PyInstaller one-folder), licence texts, a source offer and relinking
    instructions.
  - **Not used, and excluded from bundles:** QtWebEngine, Qt Quick/QML, QtNetwork, Qt Charts, Qt Graphs and Qt Data
    Visualization (the last three are GPL only).
  - **Evidence** (`docs/reports/gui/research.md` Q1):
    - PySide6 has supported 3.14 since 6.10.1, with `cp310-abi3` wheels;
    - native accessibility on all three OSes;
    - model/view virtualisation (paint cost flat from 10k to 1M rows; 100k-row model-side sort in 86 ms);
    - Graphics View with a BSP index and LOD (10k nodes interactive when zoomed in);
    - follow-system theme APIs.
  - **Amendment (2026-10-14): user decision 2026-10-14: G1–G2 build starts before the round; G3+ unchanged.** The
    build runs on branch `gui-build` (session "GUI build"); progress and deviations are in
    `docs/reports/gui/build-log.md`.
  - **Rejected:**
    - PyQt6 (GPLv3 or commercial);
    - Tkinter (no screen-reader support on the bundled Tk 8.6; Treeview has no virtual mode);
    - Textual as the main GUI (terminal; `textual serve` / textual-web are servers). It is kept as a possible later SSH
      companion;
    - Dear PyGui (no accessibility);
    - Toga (slow tables, no graph canvas);
    - Slint (Python bindings in beta; GPLv3 or attribution licence);
    - Tauri, Electron, pywebview, NiceGUI and Flet (web view, server or client/server);
    - Qt Quick/QML (AutoText default, CVE-2025-12385 guidance, deploy weight, no gain).
- **D-391 (2026-10-14, GUI placement and coupling; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).** The GUI is a **separate uv project `gui/`** (`agentprov-gui`, Python ≥ 3.14, its own
  `uv.lock`).
  - It depends one-way on `agentprov` through an **allowlist of read-only core modules** (`api`, `versions`, `formats`,
    `ingest.quote/loaders/limits`, `corpus.reader/index/register/layout`, `aer.reader`, `sem.types`,
    `render.graph/style/dot`, `adapters.registry`, `progress`).
  - The core never imports `agentprov_gui`: a new rule in `tests/boundary/test_import_boundary.py`, and no core lock lists
    the GUI or PySide6.
  - All writes are `agentprov` CLI subprocesses.
  - The GUI imports no network module (a static test plus a fresh-interpreter check).
  - **Rejected:**
    - a `gui` extra of the core (it puts Qt in the core lock);
    - calling writer APIs in-process (it duplicates the guards, and the job dies with the window);
    - no core import at all (it re-implements `quote_untrusted` and `render.graph`, splitting the G.8.2/G.8.6 rules).
- **D-392 (2026-10-14, GUI job manager; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).**
  - **Detaching:** jobs run as **detached** CLI processes:
    - POSIX: a new session;
    - Windows: `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`.
  - **Process environment:** stdout and stderr go to files, stdin is closed (or carries the keys once, D-395), and the
    environment is an allowlist.
  - **State:** each job has a directory `$AGENTPROV_HOME/gui/jobs/<uuid7>/` with `job.json` (argv, pid +
    `create_time`), progress, log, summary and control files.
  - **Lifecycle:** re-attach is from files; closing the GUI never stops a job.
  - **Serialisation:** one writer per corpus, plus global slots for `fetch`, `import --fetch` and `backends build`.
  - **Batches:** a batch queue (the regeneration round) that advances only while the GUI is open.
  - **Rejected:**
    - `QProcess` with pipes (the job dies or blocks with the GUI);
    - a scheduler daemon (a resident service);
    - a terminal multiplexer (not cross-platform).
- **D-393 (2026-10-14, core: progress channel 0.2; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).** `agentprov-progress/0.2`, additive to 0.1.
  - **New events:** `run` header, per-file `seq`, `stage` begin and end, a **`heartbeat` absolute snapshot** every 2 s,
    `worker` spawn and exit with pids, `session` (live, with the staging path), `control` acknowledgement, and
    `end.outcome`.
  - **File handling:** `--progress-file` **appends** and rotates at `--progress-max-bytes` (8 MiB, one `.1`).
  - **Gaps closed:** the T1 pool reporter is wired up, and `package` and `verify` gain stage events. Container imports
    mark `unit_kind`, so totals do not mix.
  - **Overhead** (research M1): ~1 µs per event enqueue, ~13.5 µs per line in the writer thread, plus one heartbeat
    every 2 s. That is under 0.01 % of an import.
  - **Byte-neutral:** no AER, SEM, PROV or `fn_digest` change.
  - **Rejected:**
    - parsing logs (prose; DEBUG cost);
    - polling `executions.jsonl` or `register.jsonl` (rewritten only at flush for `import`);
    - a socket or pipe protocol (a server; breaks re-attach).
- **D-394 (2026-10-14, core: control file; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).** A global writer option `--control-file PATH`, holding
  `{"format":"agentprov-control/0.1","request":"drain"|"stop","issued","nonce"}`.
  - **Polling:** the CLI checks it by `stat` at unit boundaries (≤ once per second inside long units) and echoes a
    `control` progress event.
  - **`drain`:** finishes in-flight units, flushes and exits with outcome `drained` (exit 0). It is resumable by
    re-running the same argv.
  - **`stop`:** behaves like the first SIGTERM on every OS. Windows has no graceful signal path today.
  - **Rejected:**
    - SIGSTOP/SIGCONT (wall-clock timeouts and paid HTTP calls keep running; no Windows equivalent);
    - signals only (not graceful on Windows);
    - stdin commands (no pipe may tie the job to the GUI);
    - sockets or named pipes (a server).
- **D-395 (2026-10-14, core + GUI: API keys; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).**
  - **Storage:** API keys live only in the OS keychain through `keyring`.
    - Back-ends are restricted to an allowlist: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Locker, Secret Service and KWallet.
    - `keyrings.alt`, `fail`, `null` and chainers containing them are refused, and the back-end is checked after
      loading.
    - Without an allowed back-end, real-model runs from the GUI are disabled.
  - **Entry:** keys are entered once in Settings and never shown again.
  - **Hand-off (core):** a new `run --env-stdin` reads one strict JSON object (≤ 64 KiB) from stdin before any other step.
    - It uses the same name allowlist as `endpoints.toml`.
    - It is exclusive with `--env-file`, and **it disables the default `<repo>/.env` read**.
    - The existing path then forwards only the selected key into the T2 worker environment, and registers it for
      redaction.
  - **Never:** on disk, in argv, in the T0 environment, in `job.json`, QSettings or logs. The GUI never reads `.env`.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a temporary `.env` (plain text on disk);
    - keys in the T0 environment (readable by same-user processes) or in argv;
    - QSettings;
    - an encrypted file with a master password (re-implements a keychain).
- **D-396 (2026-10-14, GUI display security; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).** Security rules S1–S14 of `docs/reports/gui/design.md` §11 apply, each enforced by tests.
  - **Plain text only:** every text widget comes from one factory (`SafeLabel` with PlainText, `safe_message_box`,
    `ReadOnlyText`). Tooltips are `Qt.convertFromPlainText(escape_untrusted_line(s))`.
    - Measured: QLabel and QMessageBox default to AutoText, and QLabel to `LinksAccessibleByMouse`.
  - **Banned by an AST lint:** `setHtml`, `setMarkdown`, `QTextBrowser`, `QGraphicsTextItem`, `Qt.RichText`/`AutoText`,
    and `openUrl` with data.
  - **Content is hidden by default, per pane** (G.8.2). Shown content goes through `quote_untrusted`. One-line labels use
    `escape_untrusted_line`; `display_clean` avoids double escaping.
  - **Nothing from data:** no links, media or HTML; artefact media are never rendered.
  - **No GUI feature forwards content to a model.**
  - **Rejected:**
    - relying on widget defaults;
    - HTML escaping alone (it misses bidi and controls);
    - content shown by default.
- **D-397 (2026-10-14, core allowlist + GUI: graph view; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).**
  - **Pipeline:**
    1. `render.graph.build_model`;
    2. DOT from `render.style` with the trusted-grammar default labels only;
    3. `dot -Tjson` under the G.8.6 process controls (**core: add `json` to `render.dot.run_dot`'s formats**) for the
       core bundle and small graphs (≤ 600 nodes or 1,500 edges; edge labels never sent to `dot`);
    4. above that, a deterministic GUI-side layered layout (cycle-breaking, longest-path ranks, barycentre sweeps):
       10 ms for the largest real all-bundle document, where `dot` needed ≥ 121 s of CPU;
    5. native `QGraphicsView` drawing with built-in C++ items and a static BSP index.
  - **Rendering:** LOD tiers, an overview raster for zoomed-out views, a collapsed view of mentions and passes, and a
    digest-keyed layout cache.
  - **"All" mode:** the core layout plus overlays (inference edges, assessment badges), or engine (b) for a full
    layout.
  - **Popover:** a plain-text attribute table, not a `QToolTip`.
  - **Rejected:**
    - SVG display (no per-element interaction; an SVG web view breaks the hard constraint);
    - `prov.dot` (it emits `URL` and `href` from data);
    - in-process Python layout;
    - force-directed layout by default (it ignores PROV time direction).
- **D-398 (2026-10-14, GUI live PROV preview; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).** **Experimental, off by default.**
  - **Process:** a separate helper at below-normal priority tails the capture/0.1 logs named by `session` progress events.
  - **Reading:** it reads **envelope metadata and ids only**, never `data` content or blobs, because staged files have
    not passed T0's secret scan.
  - **Drawing:** it builds a provisional graph with an append-only layered placement and redraws at ≤ 1 Hz.
  - **Labelling:** it is always labelled "Preview: not corpus provenance", and it is never saved or compared
    (invariant 1).
  - **Measured** (research M10): the writer's `os.write` latency is unchanged within noise, and the tailer costs ≈ 0.8 %
    of one core at 400 events/s.
  - **Rejected:**
    - running the engine in-process for a preview (heavy, and blurs invariant 1);
    - showing message content;
    - a preview that persists anything.
- **D-399 (2026-10-14, GUI packaging, names, About; approved as direction 2026-10-14 by the user, relayed by the orchestrator session; build after the regeneration round).**
  - **Development:** `uv run --project gui`.
  - **Release bundles:** **PyInstaller one-folder** bundles per OS:
    - macOS: a Developer ID-signed, hardened-runtime, notarised `.app`;
    - Windows: Authenticode-signed;
    - Linux: AppImage.
  - **Bundle checks:** a build-time check fails on excluded Qt modules. Graphviz is not bundled (the system `dot`).
  - **Writes:** always through the configured checkout's CLI, so `producer.git_commit` and the lock digest stay true.
    Without a checkout the app is viewer-only.
  - **Names:** the monitor tab is **"System"** ("Activity" is a PROV term; "Runs" is the job list).
  - **About:** the GUI and core versions, `aer/0.1`, `sem/0.1`, `capture/0.1`, `agentprov-prov/0.1`, `apv 0.1.0`,
    "MIT, free to use", "Nicholas Jones", "Developed as part of PhD research", the git commit when available, and the
    repository name as plain text with no link.
  - **Rejected:**
    - Nuitka or `pyside6-deploy` as the default (Nuitka's licence for compiled output unverified);
    - Briefcase as the default (less PySide6 track record, AppImage discouraged);
    - one-file bundles (LGPL relinking);
    - bundling a frozen CLI for writes (wrong producer provenance).
  - **Downstream of D-390..D-399** (CLAUDE.md rule 10):
    - **None** of these moves AER, SEM or PROV bytes, the compat oracle, corpus manifests or manuscript numbers.
    - D-393, D-394, D-395 and D-397 change `src/agentprov/cli/`, `progress.py`, `io/workers.py` (reporter wiring),
      `corpus/derive.py`, `corpus/package.py`, `corpus/verify.py` and `render/dot.py`. None of these files is in any stage's
      code digest, which covers `adapters/runner` + `aer` for the `aer` stage; `sem`; `prov` + `vocab`; `validate`; and
      `views` (`importer.py:1829-1864`, `derive.py:242-287`).
    - **Exception:** emitting `stage`/`unit_kind` events from `adapters/runner/importer.py` **moves the `aer` stage's
      `engine_code_sha256`** for imports made afterwards, as D-321 did. That is a `derivation.json` change for new imports,
      never an AER/SEM/PROV byte change. Under the regen-batch rule it lands before, or together with, the regeneration
      round. Alternatively, the importer events can be emitted from the CLI layer around the runner, which leaves the digest
      alone; the builder should prefer that if the needed counters are reachable there.
    - Their tests go in the core suite.
    - D-391 adds one boundary rule.
    - Everything else lives in `gui/`.
- **D-440..D-449 (2026-10-14, native macOS GUI design, branch `gui-macos-design`):** the native macOS look and behaviour
  of the desktop GUI, with Windows and Linux following their own conventions. The evidence (measured on macOS 27.0.1)
  and the design are in `docs/reports/gui/macos-design.md`, the Light/Dark mockups in `docs/reports/gui/mockups/`.
  **User decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction** (relayed by the orchestrator session and given in the session's
  own window). Nothing is built; the build comes after the regeneration round, with D-390..D-399.
- **D-440 (2026-10-14, GUI toolkit for a native macOS feel; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction; amends
  D-390).** PySide6 6.12 / Qt Widgets stays the toolkit on macOS, Windows and Linux. On macOS a **native chrome layer**
  is added through PyObjC (MIT): `pyobjc-core`, `pyobjc-framework-Cocoa` and `pyobjc-framework-UserNotifications`, as
  darwin-only dependencies of `gui/`, pinned in `gui/uv.lock`. All PyObjC use is confined to
  `agentprov_gui/platform/macos.py`. The layer provides:
  - a real `NSToolbar` (unified, Liquid Glass groups, title and subtitle, `NSSearchToolbarItem`) whose items call the
    same `QAction`s as the menus;
  - Dock tile progress;
  - `UNUserNotificationCenter` notifications;
  - the standard Window-menu actions;
  - the Reduce Transparency and Differentiate Without Colour flags.

  If the module or its smoke check fails, the GUI falls back automatically to the Qt toolbar (a setting, and
  `AGENTPROV_GUI_NATIVE_CHROME=0`).
  - **Evidence:** a Qt window with the native toolbar closely matches a SwiftUI reference (macos-design §2.1, M4 against
    M5). Tuned Qt alone reaches only the macOS 14–15 look (M3).
  - **Rejected:**
    - a SwiftUI or AppKit front-end beside Qt: two view layers; the security layer ported to Swift; full Xcode needed
      (M6); a macOS-only test stack while CI is dispatch-only (D-431); the M10 spawn risk;
    - a Swift front-end over a Python view-model helper: still two view layers plus an IPC protocol. Kept as the
      re-evaluation option;
    - a PyObjC AppKit front-end: rewrites every data source and the graph canvas;
    - wxPython: no virtual list on macOS; no Linux wheels; `wxAccessible` is MSW-only;
    - Toga: bulk-update issue #2747 is open;
    - Compose Multiplatform, Avalonia and .NET MAUI: not native on macOS; not Python; MAUI has no Linux;
    - Qt only: no glass toolbar, no Dock progress, deprecated notifications.
  - **Re-evaluate** if a Qt release breaks the toolbar attachment without a fix within one patch release, or if Qt ships
    public `NSToolbar` or glass APIs.
- **D-441 (2026-10-14, GUI main-executable SDK; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction).** The macOS release
  bundle's main executable (PyInstaller bootloader or launcher) is linked against the current macOS SDK (≥ 26). Without
  that, AppKit and Qt draw the compatibility look: the uv CPython 3.14.8 is SDK 15.0 (measured M1/M2).
  - The build checks the SDK with `otool -l` and, if needed, rebuilds the bootloader from source on the build Mac.
  - An optional development launcher (`Py_BytesMain`, about 30 lines) gives the current look under `uv run`.
  - Qt ≥ 6.12.1 on macOS 27 (QTBUG-150017).
  - **Rejected:** accepting the compatibility look; the `UIDesignRequiresCompatibility` opt-out (honoured only on macOS
    26).
- **D-442 (2026-10-14, GUI window model and HIG mapping; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction).**
  macos-design §3:
  - one main window: a sidebar with Corpora / Jobs / Release sections, content, and a trailing inspector;
  - a standard Settings window (⌘,) with a pane toolbar;
  - About in the App menu;
  - New Live Run as its own window (⌘L);
  - every R1/R2 confirmation, purge and the design §8.3a warning as sheets, with Cancel never the default;
  - a toolbar activity item for jobs instead of a bottom status strip;
  - the menu bar and shortcuts of §3.2 and §3.4.
  - **Rejected:** Settings and About as sidebar items on macOS (not HIG); the bottom status strip on macOS (the HIG
    discourages bottom bars); a modal window for Run live's consent (a sheet keeps the context); a separate tab view
    under the toolbar (segments in the toolbar, ≤ 7).
- **D-443 (2026-10-14, GUI visual system; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction).**
  - **Fonts:** system fonts only. SF Pro and SF Mono are used only through the system and never bundled (Apple font
    licence); Segoe UI Variable on Windows; Adwaita Sans, Cantarell or Noto Sans on Linux.
  - **Colour:** `QPalette` roles including Accent. Status tokens carry Light, Dark and Increase Contrast values, read
    from `NSColor` system colours on macOS.
  - **Status:** always a shape plus a word.
  - **Layout:** a 4-pt grid with the metrics of macos-design §4.3.
  - **Icons:** SF Symbols through `QIcon.fromTheme` on macOS (52 names checked present); Phosphor (MIT) bundled for
    Windows and Linux.
  - **Motion:** Reduce Motion honoured (Qt 6.12 `motionPreference`).
  - **App icon:** layered (Icon Composer), with no text and no SF Symbols.
  - **Rejected:** bundling SF fonts or exporting SF Symbols (licence); Segoe Fluent Icons off Windows (licence); Fluent
    UI System Icons everywhere (a Windows look on GNOME); Remix Icon (custom 2026 licence); colour-only status.
- **D-444 (2026-10-14, GUI PROV graph appearance and interaction; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction).**
  - **Colour:** fills keep the W3C hues in Light and Dark. Strokes use the design §12 dark variants, plus 2-px
    Increase-Contrast strokes.
  - **Selection:** an accent ring plus a doubled stroke.
  - **Hover:** a `Qt.Popup` popover with a plain-text table; a click pins it to the inspector.
  - **Zoom and pan:** pinch zooms, smart zoom toggles Fit / 100 %, two-finger scroll pans, ⌥-wheel zooms, ⌘+ ⌘− ⌘0 ⌘9;
    the zoom range is 5–800 %.
  - **Controls:** glass controls over the canvas on macOS; plain buttons elsewhere.
  - **Rejected:** wheel zoom on trackpads (not macOS behaviour); recolouring the fills for Dark (breaks the notation's
    identity colours); selection by colour only.
- **D-445 (2026-10-14, GUI platform integration; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction).**
  - **Dock:** the badge counts running jobs; tile progress through `NSDockTile`.
  - **Notifications:** `UNUserNotificationCenter` in a signed bundle, only for jobs over 2 min when the app is not
    frontmost, never carrying data text. The fallback is a Dock bounce plus an in-app banner.
  - **Windows:** multiple windows; no window tabs (Qt disallows them).
  - **State:** restored with `QSettings`, never the Show-content toggles.
  - **Full screen:** native Full Screen and tiling.
  - **Not provided:** a Quick Look or Spotlight extension.
  - **Equivalents:** taskbar progress (`ITaskbarList3`) and toasts with an AUMID on Windows; Unity `LauncherEntry` and
    freedesktop notifications over QtDBus on Linux.
  - **Rejected:**
    - `QSystemTrayIcon.showMessage` (uses the deprecated `NSUserNotification`, QTBUG-110998);
    - a Quick Look or Spotlight extension (a sandboxed Swift `.appex`, no working `CSImportExtension` on macOS, a new
      display surface for untrusted text);
    - re-enabling window tabbing behind Qt's back.
- **D-446 (2026-10-14, GUI accessibility; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction).**
  - Every widget has an accessible name, enforced by a lint.
  - The graph is exposed through an Elements list plus a custom `QAccessibleInterface` for its nodes; the list alone
    stays if the G1 VoiceOver test fails.
  - Keyboard access is complete, including graph walking by edges and Full Keyboard Access.
  - Text size is adjustable in the app from 85 to 200 % (macOS has no Dynamic Type).
  - Increase Contrast tokens apply; under Windows contrast themes only system colours are used.
  - Bundle letters are shown when Differentiate Without Colour is on.
  - **Rejected:** the Elements list alone without trying the accessible interface; a fixed font size.
- **D-447 (2026-10-14, GUI macOS packaging; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction; refines D-399).**
  - **Signing:** a Developer ID Application signature, the hardened runtime and a secure timestamp; notarised and
    stapled.
  - **Distribution:** outside the App Sandbox and the Mac App Store.
  - **Entitlements:** none to start with. Library-validation or executable-memory exceptions are added only if the
    bundle test shows a need.
  - **Keys:** entered in the signed bundle. The CLI never reads the keychain (D-395 unchanged).
  - **Evidence:**
    - a sandboxed probe could not run the venv CLI or Homebrew `dot`, or reach `~/.agentprov` (M11);
    - with temporary exceptions added, the nested `sandbox-exec` used for live containment still failed with
      `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted` (M12).
  - **Rejected:**
    - App Sandbox with temporary exceptions (breaks containment; subject to App Review discretion);
    - an embedded, inheriting helper (the CLI must be the checkout's own, D-399);
    - the Mac App Store (sandbox required; guideline 2.4.5(iii) forbids processes that outlive the app).
- **D-448 (2026-10-14, GUI security rules for the native layer; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction;
  amends D-396).**
  - **S11 amended:** `socket`/`_socket` are tolerated in `sys.modules` only when PyObjC's `objc._convenience` imported
    them, and only on macOS. `ssl`, `http.client`, `urllib.request`, `QtNetwork` and `QtWebEngine*` stay banned, and the
    static source bans are unchanged.
  - **New S15:**
    - PyObjC only in `platform/macos.py`; ctypes Windows calls only in `platform/windows.py`; QtDBus only in
      `platform/linux.py`.
    - These modules receive only fixed strings, numbers and one-line ids escaped with `escape_untrusted_line`. Never
      content, attributed strings or `NSTextView`s.
    - The `NSSearchToolbarItem` text goes only to the in-process filter model.
  - **Rejected:** dropping the `sys.modules` check (it is the runtime proof of S11); patching PyObjC to avoid `socket`
    (an unsupported fork).
- **D-449 (2026-10-14, GUI Windows and Linux conventions; user decision 2026-10-14: approved as direction; amends
  D-390's styles and design §12).**
  - **Windows 11:**
    - Qt's `windows11` style (the default since Qt 6.7); Fusion on Windows 10. This replaces design §12's Fusion on
      Windows; the earlier research had marked `windows11` *unverified*.
    - A NavigationView-style pane with Settings pinned at the bottom and About inside Settings.
    - A CommandBar, ContentDialogs, an InfoBar strip mirrored on the taskbar, and the Fluent shortcuts (F5, Ctrl+F, F6).
  - **GNOME:** a header-bar layout; a primary menu (Preferences Ctrl+,, Keyboard Shortcuts Ctrl+?, About); no menu bar;
    in-app toasts.
  - **KDE:** a menu bar (Ctrl+M), a Configure dialog (Ctrl+Shift+,), Help › About, and task-manager progress.
  - **Rejected:** the macOS layout on every platform (each platform follows its own conventions); client-side GNOME
    decorations drawn by the app (Qt Widgets uses the compositor's decorations).
  - **Downstream of D-440..D-449** (CLAUDE.md rule 10):
    - none moves AER, SEM or PROV bytes, the compat oracle, corpus manifests, any core module, the core lock or
      manuscript numbers;
    - they touch only the unbuilt `gui/` project and the GUI documents;
    - D-448 changes GUI tests only;
    - the core boundary rule (D-391) is unchanged.
- **D-410 (2026-10-14, pipeline-perf; user-approved 2026-10-14).** `aer.rules.load_catalogue` caches each parsed rule
  catalogue by `(source, sha256 of the resource bytes)`.
  - **Why:** mapping cites rules record by record, so every execution parsed the TOML about 22 times. That was 15–19% of
    an import's CPU (Mandate: 8,851 parses, 71 s of 369 s).
  - **Purity:** the bytes are read on every load, so changed bytes are parsed again; a failed parse is never cached.
    `parse_catalogue` is unchanged and a `RuleCatalogue` is immutable, so the cache is a pure function of its inputs
    (G.4.7).
  - **Effect:** the map job's CPU on Mandate fell from 58.1 s to 2.7 s.
  - **Identity:** Mandate imported before and after: 1,595 of 1,596 files byte-identical. The only difference is
    `derivation.json`'s `aer` `engine_code_sha256` and `fn_digest` (regen-batch item 32; land before part C).
  - **Rejected:** `functools.cache` on `load_catalogue` (keyed by name, it would miss changed bytes); caching inside
    `code_verification` only (the registry autoloader and `MapContext` parse too).
- **D-411 (2026-10-14, pipeline-perf; user-approved 2026-10-14).** `cli/migrate.py` imports the migration engine
  (`migration.gates`, `.pipeline`, `.lock`) when `migrate` runs, not at CLI start-up.
  - The parser is unchanged: `--help` for the root and every command is byte-identical.
  - Effect: `cli.main` import + parser 0.27 → 0.24 s.
  - **Rejected:** splitting every `cli/` module into register and handler parts. That is about 0.1 s per call against
    churn in about 15 files, and tests patch module attributes such as `fetch.Fetcher`.
- **D-412 (2026-10-14, pipeline-perf; deferrals-reviewed; user-approved 2026-10-14).** `strict_json_loads` skips work a
  byte count proves cannot raise:

- **D-315 (2026-10-14, RW-1 follow-up: objects that hold the same bytes are withheld together; F-1 of ingest-formats-3
