- **D-430 (2026-10-14, `recompute` at this package of a corpus built under other versions is a drift report; user ruling
  2026-10-14, after regeneration-plan finding F-8).** On the Mandate p10 clone, `recompute --dry-run` at main (with the
  D-31 bumps) re-mapped the `aer` stage under the current `mandate-agentdojo-eval@2` and catalogue `agentdojo` 2, while
  the recorded `agentdojo.suites@1` was replayed: 396 `changed_explained`, and an output that H.2.5 would refuse.
  - **Ruling:**
    - **Reproduction is at the building commit.** A corpus recomputes to 0 differences at the commit and core lockfile
      that built it (HL "Derivation reproducibility"), in a scratch worktree. This is the regeneration plan's D-358
      check. The commit is `producer.git_commit` (with `git_tree_clean`) where the manifest records it. The stored
      pre-round corpora do not record it: their commit is the one whose code digests (`derivation.json`
      `engine_code_sha256`, `adapter_code_sha256`) and core `uv.lock` digest match. All eight match `afe7038`, where the
      original import, repeated on the same pinned input, gave byte-identical outputs (regeneration plan §3.7).
    - **At this package it is a drift report.** `Derivation.check_inputs` lists every declared version this build would
      record differently, per recomputed stage (`version drift: aer: source profile <id> v<n> recorded, v<m> current`;
      `... catalogue <ns> v<n> recorded, v<m> current`; `sem: <ref> reads catalogue <ns> v<n>, the AER would declare
      v<m>`). A dry run prints them as notices and classifies as before (`changed_explained` where a declared version
      differs).
    - **A writing recompute refuses** (`--out`; exit 4, `corpus.derive.version_drift`) before `NEW.partial` exists: "re-import
      to upgrade, or recompute at the building commit". A corpus recorded under the current versions recomputes as before.
  - **Not built:** no legacy version gates in the mappers and no upgrade mode. Upgrading a corpus to current versions is a
    fresh re-import (the round's route (a)); an upgrade mode stays on the roadmap.
  - **Why:** replaying the recorded versions at main cannot give 0 differences. The Mandate AER bodies changed with the
    mapper code of regeneration-batch items 1-28, not only the headers, and the current mapper cites 28 `agentdojo` rules
    the archived catalogue v1 does not declare. A byte-identical replay at main would need every old mapper behaviour kept
    behind version checks.
  - **Rejected:** replaying the recorded versions in the importer (at main, old corpora fail on `RuleNotDeclared` or show
    `unexplained_change`; the user first chose it, then chose this); full legacy replay (large, permanent old code paths);
    writing the mixed corpus (H.2.5).
  - **Downstream:** moves no AER, SEM or PROV bytes, no compat output, no manifest and no manuscript number. Changes
    `corpus/derive.py` (not in any stage's code digest), `cli/derive.py` and `corpus/verify.py` (the injected current-profile
    lookup). `verify --level rederive` at main still fails on such a corpus, as it should: it is a reproduction check.
  - **Addendum (2026-10-22, pre-round review PR-3 / P-1; deferrals part C):** the record format, the corpus format and the
    `apv` vocabulary are declared versions too. `Derivation.version_drift` lists `aer: format aer/0.1 recorded, aer/0.2
    current` and `corpus: format agentprov-corpus/0.1 recorded, agentprov-corpus/0.2 current` when the `aer` stage is
    re-mapped, and `prov: vocabulary apv 0.1.0 recorded (by agentprov-corpus/0.1), apv 0.2.0 current` when PROV is
    recomputed. Any re-derivation recomputes the sem/prov/validation group, so **every writing recompute of a
    corpus/0.1 corpus is refused** at this build (`--stages validation` included), and re-import (the round's route (a))
    is the only upgrade path; a dry run reports the drift. The refusal names each drift on a line of its own, and
    `summary.refusal` carries them (P-3, re-check RC-8).
- **D-450 (2026-10-14, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, finding BF-18: archives are read decoded for the `[withhold]` byte
  rules; user decision 2026-10-14: approved).** A byte rule was searched only in every stored raw object's bytes as
  stored, and the AD-12 closure followed only `selected` member rows. A canary inside a deflated (or tar.gz / tar.zst)
  member was never seen, above all in a member the profile did not select: it is never decompressed at import (R-40)
  and has no object of its own. Neither backstop saw it either: `chain` and the deposit builder rescan the same stored
  bytes, and gitleaks runs with `--max-archive-depth 0`. So the container was released. The shipped profiles reach this:
  geminicli D.23.7 (key-shaped values in `claude_code` files the profile does not select, inside the zstd tar) and
  credleak D-265 (collector logs the profile does not select, inside the zip).
  - **Decision:**
    - **Seal-time decoded scan** (`agentprov.corpus.withhold_scan`; G.9.5 is the precise statement). When the policy
      has byte rules, the stored archives are read in decoded form. Recognition uses the first 512 and last 64 KiB
      bytes only. A zip at offset 0, a gzip or zstd tar and a split archive (through its parts) are opened. Any other
      archive or compressed-stream shape fails closed (unscanned). The bytes are copied by digest into a scratch store
      under `$AGENTPROV_HOME/tmp` and expanded by the bounded `expand` job in T1 (the G.3.5 gate, default limits).
      Every member's label and contents are scanned, and nested archives are read depth first. A member is deleted
      once read; at most `max_total_bytes` of decoded members are stored per root.
    - **Withholding.** A match withholds the archive object (basis `profile_rule`, new detector
      `agentprov-withhold-decoded/1`), at object level, and only when no other cause withholds it already, so an
      archive withheld by the closure keeps basis `container`. Its D-315 group and the archives that hold it follow.
    - **Fail closed.** An archive that cannot be read decoded refuses the seal (`corpus.withhold.unscanned`, exit 4)
      unless it is withheld for another cause. The reasons are the recognition above, a limit, a rejected or unexpected
      member, bytes after a zip's end record, nesting beyond the allowance, a missing split part, bytes that do not
      match their digest, or a worker pool that cannot start (isolation, the interpreter guard; never a crash).
    - **Backstops.** `withhold.rescan` (`verify --level chain`, the deposit builder) does the same over the released
      tree. A match is reported for the archive's label. An archive that cannot be read decoded goes to an `unscanned`
      collector: the builder refuses it (`release.refused.withhold_unscanned`). Without the collector it is reported as
      a match of the reserved rule id `<unscanned>`, which no valid rule id can equal, so `chain` fails until it maps it
      to a code of its own. That `verify.py` change is routed to ingest-formats-3 with BF-19 (`withheld.container`),
      because that branch owns the file.
    - **`release_scan.py` keeps `--max-archive-depth 0`, and now says why.** gitleaks' archive extraction is not bounded
      by the G.3 limits, so it never runs over third-party archives. AgentPROV's bounded path reads them instead.
  - **Rejected:**
    - relying on the release-time gitleaks scan (it does not open archives, and should not; D-289 also notes that many
      canaries have no recognisable shape);
    - decoding in the sealing process (archives are parsed only in T1, G.4);
    - withholding the executions of an archive whose decoded members match (they cite their own selected members, which
      are scanned as stored; withholding them all would drop every run of a deposit for one unselected file);
    - a label-based guess of which members are archives (a misnamed archive would pass unread; the first bytes decide);
    - skipping archives that cannot be read (silent release of unread bytes).
  - **Downstream:** byte class 0. No AER, SEM or PROV byte and no stage code digest moves: `corpus/` and `release/` are
    in no digest, and `raw.members` (EXPAND_MODULES) is used, not changed. `WITHHELD.json` of a future seal can now list
    an archive with the new detector. A seal can now be refused where it used to pass: a policy with byte rules over a
    corpus that stores an archive that cannot be read decoded (D-452 and D-453 narrow this; D-454 withholds the rest).
    Sealing, `chain` and the builder spend T1 time decoding the stored archives when the policy has byte rules, and a
    seal does it twice (the planner, then the seal's own `chain` run). An independent review of the first version found
    fail-open shapes (a prefixed zip, an uncompressed tar, 7z), unbounded scratch use and a crash on degraded
    isolation; all fixed before the gate. Tests: `tests/unit/corpus/test_withhold_scan.py` (scanner, planner, rescan;
    the geminicli and credleak shapes with the shipped policies) and
    `tests/adapters/geminicli/test_withhold_e2e.py::test_a_key_in_an_unselected_member_withholds_the_tar_d450` (import,
    seal, `chain --release`, deposit).
- **D-451 (2026-10-14, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, finding BF-33: stage code digests cover each stage's import closure;
  user decision 2026-10-14: approved, held for the regeneration round).** The sem, prov and validation
  `engine_code_sha256` scopes are fixed directory lists (`corpus/derive.py` and `adapters/runner/importer.py`, pinned
  equal). The code those stages run imports modules outside them: `adapters/agentdojo/citation.py`, `history_table.py`,
  `adapters/code_verification.py`, `adapters/dtap/matcher.py`, `aer/evidence.py`, `aer/reader.py`, `aer/rules.py`. So
  `recompute --out` (reuse on by default) carries stale SEM/PROV outputs after a behaviour edit there, and reports them
  identical.
  - **Decision:** pin each stage's file list as the transitive import closure of its entry modules: a constant shared by
    both files, with a test that recomputes the closure (ast) and fails when it grows past the list.
  - **Held:** it moves every recorded stage code digest (byte class 1). It is built on a held branch (`bugpass-regen`)
    after the twins' `corpus/derive.py` work and ingest-formats-3's importer work have landed, and is not pushed until
    the regeneration round. The class-0 stop-gap in `_reuse_corpus_key` (also compare the aer stage's
    `adapter_code_sha256` and `engine_code_sha256`) belongs to the twins session.
  - **Rejected:** keeping the fixed lists (silent stale reuse); hashing the whole package (any edit anywhere would
    invalidate every reuse).
  - **Built (branch `bugpass-regen-d451`, held).** `agentprov.stage_scopes` (layer 0) holds the seeds and the pinned
    closures; `tests/unit/test_stage_scopes.py` recomputes them by ast and fails on growth or a stale entry.
    `prov/specs.py` reaches `prov/compat/adprov_v2_3` lazily for the oracle's `SPEC`/`NOTICE`; the compat package stays
    excluded (`PROV_EXCLUDE`), as before, since it is frozen and is its own stage. Byte impact: the `sem`, `prov` and
    `validation` `engine_code_sha256` and `fn_digest` in `derivation.json` of every corpus imported or derived
    afterwards; no AER, SEM, PROV, validation, index, register or manifest byte. Stored corpora reuse nothing across
    the change (their recorded digests differ), so the first `recompute --out` after it recomputes those stages.
  - **Addendum (2026-10-21, finding BF-39; user decision 2026-10-21: extend to `expand` now, design the `aer` scope
    first).** D-451 covered sem, prov and validation only. Two more stage digests have the same gap:
    - **`expand`.** `raw.members.EXPAND_MODULES` was a hand-kept list of 8 files, while the import walk from
      `raw/members.py` reaches 19. Among the 11 unhashed were `raw/origins.py`, `raw/store.py`, `raw/carve.py`,
      `ingest/paths.py` and `ingest/loaders.py`.
    - **Built.** `EXPAND_MODULES` is now `raw/members.py` plus its import closure, and
      `test_the_expand_digest_covers_the_import_closure_of_raw_members` recomputes it.
    - **Why the list stays in `raw/members.py`.** Importing it from `agentprov.stage_scopes` would put the pin file
      itself into the expand and agentdojo sem closures, so every pin edit would move those digests.
    - **D-222.** Once D-222 (carve-span) lands, `raw/origins.py` no longer imports `raw/carve.py`. Both pins then lose
      `raw/carve.py`, and the test prints the new tuples.
    - **Byte impact:** the `expand` `fn_digest` and `engine_code_sha256` in `derivation.json`, and the `fn_digest` of
      every `raw/members.jsonl` row (so the manifest's `members` digest), of every container corpus imported or
      re-derived afterwards (class 1, held with D-451). Recompute of a container corpus built before the change
      reports its member rows as relabelled by a code-only expand change, as a notice (integration review P-2). Before
      the P-2 fix it exited 1 on every archive corpus.
    - **`aer` (user decision 2026-10-21: approved as proposed).** The `aer` digest hashed `["adapters/runner", "aer"]`.
      A closure seeded at the whole runner reaches 79 files, every later stage's engine included, because the importer
      drives all stages.
      - **Scope (`stage_scopes.aer_scope(family)`).** Both directories stay hashed. Imports are followed only from the map
        path (`adapters/runner/__init__.py`: `job_map`, `map_unit`, `seal_outcome`) and `aer/`, which reaches 23 files
        (`AER_CLOSURE`: `raw/carve.py`, `raw/origins.py`, `raw/store.py`, `io/workers.py`, the archive readers, ...).
      - **Not followed:** `importer.py`, `session.py`, `live.py` and `provjob.py` are hashed, but orchestrate the sem,
        prov, validation and corpus code, which has its own digests. The runner's lazy re-export of the importer is
        not followed either.
      - **Per family.** `AER_FAMILY_CLOSURE` adds what each family's code imports from outside `adapters/<family>/`
        (3 to 11 files; adprov reaches `views/transcript_v1.py`). `adapter_code_sha256` keeps its meaning, the family
        directory.
      - **Wiring and tests.** The importer records the scope, and the BF-33 stop-gap (`derive._aer_code_unchanged`)
        compares the same scope. `tests/unit/test_stage_scopes.py` recomputes the core closure and every family's.
      - **D-222.** After it lands, `raw/carve.py` imports `ingest/jsonspan.py`, which joins `AER_CLOSURE`.
      - **Byte impact:** the aer `engine_code_sha256` and `fn_digest` in `derivation.json` (class 1, held).
- **D-452 (2026-10-14, bug pass bugpass-perf-10: the decoded scan honours the declared nesting and the corpus's own
  member objects; user decision 2026-10-14: approved, folded into D-450 before its gate).** Found by phase 10p-holds on
  `controlarena-persistent` v2. D-450 walked each archive from the top under the global `max_archive_depth` 2 and
  re-read every member. So split zip > `logs/*.zip` > `.eval` (level 3, declared by `[[import.nested]]` `max_depth = 3`)
  was unscanned. Nested zips stored under a declared raise above the global member bound (D-382, D-383) were refused
  by the scan's own gate. And every member the import had stored was decompressed again.
  - **Decision:**
    - The walk selects exactly the members the corpus does not store as objects of their own (their labels in
      `raw/members.jsonl`; all members of an archive the import never expanded).
    - A stored member is read as its own root and counts as covered only when the expansion sees its size and CRC-32.
      So a doctored `raw/members.jsonl` cannot hide a member: its bytes are read through the container.
    - The walk honours the profile's largest declared `[[import.nested]]` `max_depth`, clamped by the ceiling. It
      travels in the parsed `[withhold]` policy (`WithholdPolicy.archive_depth`, not recorded in `WITHHELD.json`), so
      the seal, `chain` and the builder read it from the same profile copy.
  - **Rejected:** a blanket depth of the ceiling (it would read archives deeper than the profile declares); re-reading
    stored members through their containers (it decompresses every expanded deposit twice and trips `max_total_bytes`
    on multi-GB split zips).
  - **Downstream:** byte class 0 (corpus/ only). For 10p, the nested zips, the good `.eval` logs and the 36 D-345 holds
    are stored objects, each read decoded as its own root; zero-byte members count as scanned.
- **D-453 (2026-10-14, bug pass bugpass-perf-10: a partial decoded scan of zips with no central directory; user
  decision 2026-10-14: approved as a follow-up).** 10p stores 186 `.eval` members cut at 256 KiB with no central
  directory, which `expand` rejects, so the decoded scan reports them unscanned.
  - **Decision:**
    - A new bounded T1 reader, used only when `expand` rejects an archive structurally. It walks the local file headers
      in order. Stored entries are read by size; deflate entries are streamed through zlib up to their end or the
      truncation, under `max_member_bytes` and the ratio limits. Nothing is stored. On a bad header it resyncs to the
      next local header.
    - Encrypted entries, other methods and stored entries of unknown size stay unscanned.
    - The object counts as `scanned_partial` (a seal-report count, nothing stored). The same job kind will also scan a
      tar's header fields and padding, which `expand` does not return.
  - **Soundness:** every byte is raw-scanned anyway. The walk decodes everything a local-header reader can reach, a
    superset of what any central-directory reader recovers. Content past a cut does not exist, and compressed bytes
    that no valid header introduces are presented as content by no zip reader.
  - **Sequencing:** it needs one `JOB_KINDS` entry in `io/workers.py` (in no digest; owned by the bf19-bf15 follow-up),
    so it is built on a fresh branch from main after that lands, with a full suite. Byte class 0.
  - **Rejected:** treating these archives as documents (fail open); decoding in the sealing process (G.4).
  - **Built (2026-10-21, branch `bugpass-d453-d454`, with D-454).** T1 job `zip_local` (`corpus/zip_local.py`, one
    `JOB_KINDS` entry). `withhold_scan` runs it when `expand` rejects a zip whole with `ingest.archive.format`, `.cd` or
    `.overlap` and the zip has a local header at offset 0, at any nesting level. Decoded entries are members like
    `expand`'s (names and data scanned, archives queued); a deflate stream that breaks gives what it decoded and the
    walk resyncs. `DecodedScan.partial`, the plan's `partial` and the seal counter `scanned_partial`. The tar header
    fields and padding are not part of this build (still not read). Byte class 0 (`corpus/`, `io/workers.py`).
- **D-454 (2026-10-14, bug pass bugpass-perf-10: archives that stay unreadable are withheld, not refused; user
  decision 2026-10-14: option (i) approved, (ii) rejected).**
  - **Decision:** an archive the decoded scan still cannot read is withheld automatically, instead of refusing the seal:
    basis `unscanned`, reason the policy's reason. A new ledger version `agentprov-withheld/0.3` and its schema file
    carry the new basis; `/0.1` and `/0.2` are unchanged (D-163). `chain` and the builder accept it.
  - **Spread:** AD-12 closes it over the archives that hold it, at object level only. The good members, stored as
    objects of their own, and their executions stay released.
  - **Reporting:** the seal report prints the count and the container chain loudly.
  - **Sequencing:** built with or before D-453; until then an unreadable archive refuses the seal (D-450).
  - **Rejected:**
    - (ii) an identity rule in `[withhold]` (objects by digest or member label): every residual would have to be listed
      by hand, a version bump of each such profile is needed, and a missed one still refuses (maintenance cost and
      miss risk);
    - refusing for ever (a source with one unreadable file could never be sealed);
    - releasing unread bytes.
  - **Built (2026-10-21, branch `bugpass-d453-d454`).** `withheld.py`: `FORMAT_03`, `BASES_03` (`unscanned` last, so
    any other cause of the object names the basis), `schemas/withheld-0.3.schema.json`; `/0.3` exactly when an entry is
    `unscanned`. `withhold.py`: the planner adds the cause with `UNSCANNED_NOTE` and the byte rules' first reason, then
    closes the containers; `WithholdPlan.unscanned` lists each chain and code. The seal report's counter
    `withheld_unscanned` and a notice starting `WITHHELD UNREAD`. `chain` and the builder need no change: they rescan
    released objects only, and the ledger reader takes `/0.3`. Byte class 0: only seals made afterwards that hold such an
    archive differ (they now seal instead of refusing).
- **D-457 (2026-10-15, bug pass bugpass-perf-10: the release scan reports third-party account paths; user decision
  2026-10-15: approved).**
  - **Context:** `tools/release_scan.py` searched only for the operator's own home path and host name (R-51, rules
    `home-path` and `host-name`; inside archives since D-491). The corpus pre-check found a third-party workstation
    account path in 24 raw-store context artefacts (`run_manifest.json`) of `interbolt-agentdojo` (PC-05, CC-11), in no
    AER, SEM or PROV statement. The release scan would have passed them with no finding. The user decided on
    2026-10-15 that account or workstation paths in raw-store context and auxiliary files are security findings: they
    are triaged before a deposit and withheld (`personal_data`) where they identify a person (D-456 withholds the
    interbolt files).
  - **Decision:**
    - A new rule `account-path` in the path scan, over every file it reads: every raw-store object (context and
      auxiliary files included, binary or not) and the decoded unselected archive members (D-491, same locators and the
      same fail-closed `home-path-unscanned` finding). The path scan becomes version 3.
    - Forms (bytes, case-sensitive unless stated): `/Users/<name>`, `/home/<name>`, their JSON forms with an escaped
      slash `\/Users\/<name>` and `\/home\/<name>`, `C:\Users\<name>`, its JSON-escaped form `C:\\Users\\<name>`,
      `C:/Users/<name>` (any drive letter, either case; `Users` in any case) and `/mnt/<drive>/Users/<name>` (WSL).
      `<name>` is `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}`, so a match is bounded and never backtracks badly.
    - Ending: the name is followed by a separator (`/`, or `\`, which also opens a JSON escape such as `\/`, `\"` or
      `\n`), a closing quote (`"`, `'`), whitespace, `,`, `:`, `;`, `)`, `]`, `}`, a NUL or the end of the file
      (the scan reads a file's last bytes once more with a NUL after them). So a bare home (`"HOME": "/Users/<name>"`,
      `HOME=/home/<name>` at the end of a file) is reported. Trailing dots are ignored for the allowlist and the
      operator check (`/home/user.` ends a sentence).
    - Speed: the search finds the literals `users`, `/home/` and `\/home\/` and matches anchored at them (some 100 to
      350 MB/s on JSON, plain or with escaped slashes).
    - Boundary: `/Users/` and `/home/`, and the escaped `\/Users\/` and `\/home\/`, must start an absolute path (not
      preceded by a letter, digit, `.`, `_` or `-`). `https://example.com/home/page/` (escaped or not) is not reported;
      `file:///Users/x/` and `"/home/x/` are.
    - Not covered: deeper roots that the boundary excludes, such as `/var/home/<name>` (Fedora Silverblue) and
      `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/<name>` (the macOS data volume), and the WSL form with escaped slashes.
    - A finding is untriaged and holds the path, rule and line only (`<path>:account-path:<line>`), never the name,
      the match or the line text.
    - Triage reuses the existing values (no new value, so `agentprov.release` is unchanged): `real` for a path that
      identifies a person (withheld `personal_data` in a new version, so `WITHHELD.json` names it), `synthetic-benchmark`
      for a made-up benchmark account, `false-positive` for text that is no account path.
    - The operator's own home path, when it is `/Users/<name>` or `/home/<name>` written unescaped, bare or not, stays
      `home-path` only. The same name in a Windows or `\/`-escaped form is an `account-path` finding, because
      `home-path` does not see it.
  - **Allowlist:** `ACCOUNT_ALLOWLIST` (a frozenset in `tools/release_scan.py`, compared case-insensitively), names
    that identify nobody: `user`, `users`, `ubuntu`, `runner`, `runneradmin`, `root`, `shared`, `guest`, `vscode`,
    `codespace`, `jovyan`, `ec2-user`, `admin`, `administrator`, `default`, `public`, `travis`, `circleci`,
    `appveyor`, `vagrant`, `docker`, `app`, `node`, `nobody`, and the placeholders `<user>`, `<username>`, `username`,
    `$user`, `%username%`, `you`, `me`, `name`, `example`. Placeholders with characters outside the name class never
    match it; they are listed so that the list stays right if the class is widened. Names made of dots only (`..`) are
    not reported either.
  - **Rejected:**
    - keeping the operator-only search (it cannot see anyone else's account, the interbolt case);
    - no allowlist (CI and container paths such as `/home/runner/` and `/Users/runner/` would flood the triage and
      hide the identifying few);
    - withholding automatically from the scan (the scan is a report outside `src/`; whether a path identifies a person
      is a human triage decision, and withholding belongs to sealing, H.4.5).
  - Byte class 0 (`tools/` and docs).
- **D-455 (2026-10-15, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, routed R-10j-3: URL download pins as archive inputs; user decision
  2026-10-15: approved).** Phase 10j's `dca` corpus is one Figshare file pinned by `url`, and only Zenodo and Hugging
  Face download pins were archive inputs (D-200), so it could not be imported.
  - **Decision:** `DOWNLOAD_PIN_KINDS` gains `url`. `ArchiveTree` builds the origin `url {url, retrieved}`; `_pin_record`
    and `import --fetch`/`--input` follow; the seal builds `{kind: url, url, retrieved_at}` (H.2.3, `retrieved_at`
    REQUIRED because the origin is mutable). It is the same extraction-free, SHA-256- and size-checked path, with the
    network only under `--allow-network`.
  - **The retrieval time:** only from the recorded fetch, the fetch cache's acquisition record (read back on a cache
    hit too), else the pin's own `retrieved_at` (RFC 3339 UTC). With neither the import is refused
    (`raw.origin.unpinned`, exit 3; invariant 2). It is never the time of the import or a file time. The object origin
    keeps the date (`retrieved`, aer/0.1), the snapshot the full time. A pin with a date-only `retrieved` key is
    refused the same way, even beside a valid `retrieved_at`.
  - **The shipped pin:** `dca-agentdojo` records `retrieved_at = "2026-10-11T09:46:41Z"`, the phase-10c acquisition
    record of the pinned bytes (sha256, size and md5 equal), replacing the date-only `retrieved` of the dropped
    duplicate D-580. In-place D-31 (version stays 1): no corpus records the profile.
  - **Not covered:** a URL archive in byte parts (refused; split archives are pinned on Zenodo or Hugging Face).
  - **Byte class 1:** `adapters/runner/` moves the `aer` stage's code digests (regen-batch item 101); no stored corpus
    has a `url` snapshot, so no AER, SEM or PROV byte moves. Held on `bugpass-regen-d455`.
  - **Rejected:** stamping the import time (an invented timestamp); a date-only `retrieved_at` (the sealed origin needs
    RFC 3339 UTC, and a time of day must not be filled in); keeping URL pins `agentprov fetch` only (the source could
    never be sealed with a pinned origin).

- **D-456 (2026-10-15, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, pre-check PC-05: interbolt-agentdojo withholds the files that carry a
  third-party account path; user decision 2026-10-15: approved, the pattern rule).** 24 `runs/published/**/run_manifest.json`

  - **D-31:** v2 with v1 archived (owner's ruling: two pre-check scratch corpora record v1). Byte class 1: the AER
    header's profile version and digest move for every interbolt AER (the 7 phase-10d fixture pins re-pinned); no
    stored corpus records the profile. Regen-batch item 104; held branch `bugpass-regen-d456`.
  - **Tests:** `tests/adapters/agentdojo/test_interbolt_withhold_e2e.py` imports a synthetic snapshot in release mode
    with the shipped profile, seals it and runs `verify --level chain --release`: the manifest with a test-made path is
    withheld (`profile_rule`, `personal_data`, no execution), the clean one and both runs are released, no sealed byte
    holds the path, the sidecar does.
  - **Rejected:** exact-label or digest rules (D-454 (ii) rejected identity rules); excluding the manifests from the
    import (D-345's route; they are evidence of how the runs were made, and the digest is to be kept); releasing them.
- **D-460 (2026-10-14, `aer.rules.drift`: corpora built while a catalogue was edited in place; follow-up of D-430,
  approved by the user 2026-10-14).** Between `afe7038` (which built every stored corpus) and the D-31 bumps
  (`430a2dc4`), catalogues were edited in place at version 1. A corpus imported in that window records, for example,
  `agentdojo` 1 with bytes that differ from the archived v1, and its AERs cite rules that v1 lacks. On main, `validate`
  then failed every row with `aer.rule.missing` and `aer.rule.class`, and tier 4 with `pv.linkage.method`: wrong
  findings for a version problem. The one known case is pipeline-perf's scratch Mandate import at `8e6d632f`.
  - **Rule:** `corpus.authority.catalogue_drift` lists the `aer` stage catalogues recorded at a shipped version whose
    `derivation.json` digest differs from the package bytes. Each one is reported once as `aer.rules.drift` ("built
    against catalogue bytes that differ from the shipped vN; check at the building commit"), in place of
    `rules.mismatch`:
    - **`validate`:** one notice per catalogue, the counter `rules_drift`, `issues_by_code`. Every row whose AER
      declares that version gets the single failing check `aer.rules.drift`; its AER-rule, SEM and tier-4 checks do
      not run.
    - **`verify`:** chain reports it as failed. `rederive` does not re-derive, and reports `rederive.unavailable`
      (unverified) per catalogue.
    - **`recompute`:** it is a D-430 drift line. A dry run reports it; `--out` refuses.
  - **Unchanged:** a swapped `rules/` copy or source or semantics profile digest is still `rules.mismatch`; the round's
    fresh re-imports are not affected; no AER, SEM or PROV bytes move. Tests: a drift-window fixture (the AERs resealed
    to declare `agentdojo` 1, the recorded digest set to today's bytes), shown to give the per-rule errors without the
    gate.
  - **Rejected:** keeping the per-rule errors and adding a note (they are wrong, not just noisy); loading the recorded
    bytes from the corpus `rules/` copy (AD-14: the package is the authority, a copy is a record).
- **D-461 (2026-10-14, bug-pass fixes BF-19 and BF-15, routed from `bugpass-perf-10`; user decision 2026-10-14: approved, relayed by the orchestrator session).**
  - **BF-19 (security).** `verify --level chain` re-checks the AD-12 container closure of withheld members. It walks
    `raw/members.jsonl` upward from every object `WITHHELD.json` lists, through every level, and a released container
    of one is `withheld.container`. Before this, a container put back into a sealed tree while dropped from
    `WITHHELD.json` passed `chain --release`, and because it was deflated the rule rescan missed the member's bytes in it
    (`repro/BF-19_B-2`). The seal already withheld such containers (`corpus/withhold.py`, D-232); only the re-check
    was missing. Test: `tests/security/test_sec25_withhold_container.py`.
  - **BF-15.** `max_split_parts` drops from 64 to 32. The expand job holds every part open (D-243) and a worker may hold
    64 descriptors (`RLIMIT_NOFILE`, G.4.3), so split archives of 59 to 64 parts always failed, reported as
    `worker.input.missing` (`repro/BF-15_A-2`). 32 parts of 256 MiB are `max_split_bytes`, and the largest observed
    split has 8 parts. A worker that runs out of descriptors now reports `worker.input.nofile`. Tests:
    `tests/unit/raw/test_split_parts_nofile.py` (the invariant `max_split_parts` + 16 ≤ `nofile`, a split at the limit
    through a real worker, and the error code).
  - **Rejected:**
    - raising `RLIMIT_NOFILE` (it would weaken the G.4.3 worker containment, a setting with its own basis);
    - opening parts lazily or re-opening them without re-hashing (a second check-then-use window, and more code in the
      worker for no observed source).
  - **Downstream:** `ingest/limits.py` is an `EXPAND_MODULES` file and `IngestLimits` changes, so the `expand`
    `fn_digest` moves for every archive or container corpus at its next import, as does `limits_sha256` (a notice only
    since the D-31 addendum). No AER, SEM or PROV byte changes. `corpus/verify.py` and `io/workers.py` are in no stage
    digest. Regen-batch entry `bugpass BF-19/BF-15`.
- **D-462 (2026-10-14, local CI is the default gate; GitHub CI is optional per repository variables; updates D-431;
  user request relayed by the orchestrator, number from `tools/reserve_id.py`).**
  - **Local CI.** `tools/ci_local.py` runs the jobs of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on this machine, with the same job
    ids, plus the local gates `generated`, `pins` and `readme-sources`. Its `core` job is the merge gate itself (the
    full suite through `tools/suite_queue.py -- pytest -n 10 --dist loadgroup -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider`) plus
    mypy, on this machine's OS only.
  - **Network and dispatch jobs.** Jobs that download (`live-run`, `dependencies`, `old-vs-new`,
    `backend-autodojo`) run only with `--allow-network`, after the user's yes. The dispatch-only jobs need
    `--with-dispatch-jobs`. Environment syncs run `--offline` otherwise and report "needs network" rather than
    failing.
  - **Options and exit code.** `--only` and `--skip` select jobs. The exit code is 0 only if every job that ran
    passed; `--strict` (releases, K.19.1) also fails on a skipped or unavailable job. A test keeps the job table in
    step with `ci.yml` (job ids, dispatch-only jobs, lockfiles, markers).
  - **Callers.** The merge train's default gate is `ci_local.py`, with every default job including `secrets`. Until
    the `.gitleaksignore` below was in place, it skipped `secrets`.
  - **GitHub CI switches.** `ci.yml` regains `push` (main) and `pull_request`, but every job is gated:
    `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || vars.CI_ON_PUSH == 'true'`. The three dispatch-only jobs keep
    `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`. With the repository variable `CI_ON_PUSH` unset or not `true`,
    a push or pull request starts a run whose jobs are all skipped: no minutes and no failure email.
    `gh variable set CI_ON_PUSH --body true|false` flips it, with no code edit.
  - **Self-hosted runner.** `CI_RUNNER`, when set to a self-hosted label, moves every job to that runner. The core
    matrix then becomes {self-hosted, `windows-latest`}; the Windows leg always stays GitHub-hosted. The Mac Studio
    is the intended self-hosted runner; it is noted, not set up.
  - **Tests.** `tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py` allows only those two job gates, and evaluates them to show
    that no job can run on push or pull request while `CI_ON_PUSH` is off.
  - **Rejected:** keeping dispatch-only (D-431 as it was): it can never run on push, even when minutes allow;
    a workflow-level `if` (GitHub has none; job-level gates are the supported switch); deriving `ci_local`'s job list
    by interpreting `ci.yml` steps (runner-specific actions such as gitleaks-action and osv-scanner-action have no
    local equivalent to execute). The job table plus a sync test is explicit.
  - **Found on the first run, and accepted (user decision 2026-10-14).** The `secrets` job reported 4 historical false
    positives in 2026-10-12 commits:
    - the word "placeholder" quoted in DECISIONS.md and `docs/reports/phase10k/trials.md`;
    - fake headers in `backends/agentdojo/tests/test_probe.py`;
    - key-shaped negatives in the hygiene test.

    They are only ever shown masked. `.gitleaksignore` holds exactly those four commit-pinned fingerprints
    (`commit:path:rule:line`), which cannot hide a new key. `tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py` refuses any other
    form, and any fingerprint whose commit does not hold the named file. A fifth acceptance needs a new decision.
- **D-480 (2026-10-14, core review D finding CD-3; user decision 2026-10-14: approved).** The generic profile check of
  `[import] variant_labels` names no family's variant.
  - **Problem.** `adapters/profiles.py` exempted the literal DRIFT variant `drift.k18.conversations` from the rule that a
    label names a declared variant, for every family (invariant 5: family logic in the core). The exemption existed only
    so that `agentdyn.profile.toml` can label part `d`, which DRIFT's import serves (`repro/D1-3`).
  - **Rule.** A label may name a variant that `[import] variants` does not declare only when the label is not one of the
    profile's own `[profile] parts`: such an entry records which other part, served by another import, the variant
    belongs to. A label giving an undeclared variant one of the profile's own parts is a `ProfileError`, as before.
    D.6.12 item 12 states it. Tests: `tests/adapters/test_profile_variant_labels.py` and the adjusted case in
    `tests/adapters/agentdojo/test_profile_machinery.py`.
  - **Rejected:** an explicit `[import]` list of label-only variants (it changes the AgentDyn profile bytes, so
    `profile_sha256` and the AER headers of every AgentDyn corpus; class 1 for no gain in checking); moving the check
    into the agentdojo family schema (the rule is generic, and other families would keep no check).
  - **Downstream:** none in stored bytes. `adapters/profiles.py` is in no stage digest; both AgentDyn profile versions
    still load unchanged. A profile that labelled an undeclared variant with a foreign part is now accepted for every
    family, not only for the DRIFT name.
- **D-481 (2026-10-14, core review D finding CD-4; user decision 2026-10-14: approved). A part served through another
  source does not count its registration in the coverage phrase.**
  - **Problem.** `coverage_phrase()` counted every registration with a counted `source` part, so AutoDojo counted through
    `rope-slice` (`via = "rope"`, corpus `rope`), whose logs are imported, owned and counted under ROPE. The phrase said
    7 sources; NC-AUTO-01 forbids presenting AutoDojo as a distinct corpus, and the `c3-coverage` gate counts over the
    pinned corpora, which give 6 (`repro/D1-4`).
  - **Rule.** I.5.6 rule 2: N excludes parts with `via` set; K is unchanged (the via part's dialect is counted through the
    serving source). Test: `tests/adapters/registry/test_claims.py::test_a_part_served_through_another_source_does_not_count_its_registration`.
  - **Rejected:** keeping N = 7 and reconciling NC-AUTO-01 and `c3-coverage` with it (it counts executions twice).
  - **Downstream: moves a manuscript number.** `all/coverage_phrase` and `all/n_sources_with_executions` drop from 7 to 6
    sources (3 formats unchanged). No AER, SEM or PROV bytes; `adapters/registry/claims.py` is in no stage digest.
- **D-490 (2026-10-14, core review B finding CB-14; user decision 2026-10-14: approved, confirmed in the review session).
  Deposit verify checks each datasheet copy against the archived `DATASHEET.md`.**
  - **Problem.** `release/verify.py` checked each `documents[]` file only against the deposit manifest, which nothing
    anchors. A forged `DATASHEET-<id>.md` (the human-facing licence, restrictions and untrusted-content statement,
    REP-3) passed `verify --release --root-digest`, and so did an extra document whose name matched the grammar
    (`docs/reports/review-core-b/findings.md`, CB-14).
  - **Rule.**
    1. `documents[]` is exactly `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `deposit-metadata.json` and one `DATASHEET-<corpus_id>.md`
       per `corpora[]` entry; anything else is `deposit.manifest.invalid`.
    2. The copy is compared with the `DATASHEET.md` read from that corpus's archives. That file is covered by the
       archived checksums and the root digest.
    3. Without mixed licence classes the copy must be byte-equal. With them it must be the sealed text, a newline and
       the builder's note. **Amended by D-620 (2026-10-22):** the note is rebuilt in full and compared byte for byte,
       not only its header.
    4. A mismatch is `deposit.document.datasheet`.
    5. `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `deposit-metadata.json` stay covered only by the deposit manifest (H.10.3).
  - **Rejected:** keeping the documents manifest-only (D-38 item 5 as written); a verified `--root-digest` would then
    vouch for a datasheet it never covered.
  - **Downstream:** none in stored bytes. `release/` is in no stage digest; builder-made deposits, single-class and
    mixed-class, verify as before.
- **D-491 (2026-10-14, core review B finding CB-16; user decision 2026-10-14: approved, confirmed in the review session;
  build after D-450 lands). The release scan reads unselected archive members for the home path and host name.**
  - **Problem.** `tools/release_scan.py` `path_scan` (R-51, G.9.4) searches stored bytes only, and gitleaks runs at
    `--max-archive-depth 0`. So a home path inside an unselected compressed member of a stored container gets through
    with no finding, for example Inspect `_journal/start.json`, the geminicli zstd tar or the credleak zip. Selected
    members are scanned as their own objects.
  - **Rule.**
    1. Archive objects are recognised by their magic bytes.
    2. Their not-selected members are streamed through the same needle search, reusing D-450's decoded-member scan
       (`corpus/withhold_scan`) in a bounded job with no extraction to disk.
    3. A hit is reported as `<label>#<member index>`, so the fingerprint stays value-free.
    4. An archive that cannot be decoded within the limits is an untriaged `home-path-unscanned` finding, so the scan
       fails closed.
    5. `PATH_SCAN_VERSION` is bumped.
  - **Rejected:** raising gitleaks' archive depth (it has no home-path rule and does not read zstd tars).
  - **Downstream:** none in stored bytes (`tools/`); a release scan of a container corpus may list new findings to
    triage.
- **D-470 (2026-10-14, phase 10q: the results-container dialect and reader; user decision 2026-10-14: approved).**
  memo-ozdincer/agentdojo (rank 6, D-146) holds its runs in whole-file JSON containers: `label`, `suite`, `model`,
  `n_results`, `aggregate`, a `results` list, and some of `adapter`, `defense`, `attack`, `mode`, `base_url`, `port`,
  `elapsed_seconds`. They are read by a new dialect `agentdojo.results_container` with a new reader
  `ResultsContainerReader` (`adapters/agentdojo/results_reader.py`) that declares `multi_execution = True` (D-320).
  - The reader yields one located item per `/results/<i>`, whose value is `{container, row}`; `container` holds the
    top-level keys except `results` and `aggregate`.

    (with or without `classification`; smoke rows add `suite`).
  - `n_results` is checked against the list length.
  - A container with an unknown row key set is sealed degenerate (`unsupported_variant`), never dropped.

  Census: `docs/reports/phase10q/README.md` §2.
  - **Rejected:** a TraceLogger variant (the file is no TraceLogger object, and a whole-file variant cannot yield
    several executions); container mode (D-320 rejected it for whole files); streaming (the largest container is 4.5 MB).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-21, as built; user decision 2026-10-21 on the new-families bug pass, NF-9).** The located
    item's value is the whole parsed container, `aggregate` included; the locator `/results/<i>` selects the row, and
    `ext.rescont.container` keeps only the listed top-level fields (D.6.20 items 1 and 4). The code, the table, D.6.20
    and the census agree; only the `{container, row}` wording above described an earlier draft.

- **D-414 (2026-10-14, pipeline-perf; reviewed by the runner, deferrals and ingest-formats-3 sessions; user-approved
  2026-10-14 with regen-batch item 42).** The parent holds the frames of worker results as bytes, not as decoded
  objects.
  - **Storage:** every `JSON` frame is still parsed and checked on arrival, then kept as its bytes (`_Payload`), in
    memory while the job's `SPOOL_MEMORY_PER_JOB` and the pool's `SPOOL_MEMORY_PER_POOL` (256 MiB) allow, otherwise in
    one spool file per `WorkerPool.run` batch.
  - **The spool file:** opened on the first spill, unlinked at creation, `pwrite` under a lock, `pread`-only reads,
    refcounted and finalized, so a consumer that raises mid-batch leaks nothing. Members above
    `MemberOutput.SPOOL_MAX` (now 1 MiB) or over budget are ranges of the same file: one descriptor per batch.
  - **Two passes:** the importer reads a `map` result in two passes (`summarise_unit_frames`, then
    `iter_unit_frames`). The whole-file, per-item, container and live-session paths keep the D-321/D-323/D-218 order
    and the same raises. `JobResult.json` is always memoised, and the per-item and container paths never use it.
  - **Effect:** parent RSS 1,191 → 674 MiB on a 7,200-execution synthetic multi-execution deposit.
  - **Identity:** byte identity on that deposit, Mandate and a ROPE subset. The only change is the aer stage's code
    digest (item 42).
  - **Design and results:** `docs/reports/pipeline-perf/parent-frames-design.md`, `results.md` §5.

- **D-415 (2026-10-21, pipeline-perf; worker-count calibration; user decision 2026-10-21: the slot default is every
  logical CPU, and the D-554 constants stay as built).** A pool with a D-554 charge policy and no `--jobs`
  (`validate --corpus`, `derive`/`recompute`, `import --size-hints`) runs one worker per logical CPU
  (`io.workers.ADMISSION_DEFAULT_SLOTS = "cpus"`). Memory admission still gates every job. Pools without a policy keep
  `resolve_worker_count(0)`.
  - **Calibration:** run at `main` 2663d44d as one exclusive queue ticket (10 CPUs, load 3–4). The data is in
    `~/.agentprov/migration-work/pipeline-perf/calib2/`. ROPE, first 1,500 executions, M2 Max (8P+4E, 32 GB):

    | Workers | Wall | vs 6 | Worst job, share of time cap | Process-tree peak |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | 3 | 476 s | 0.55× | 2.0% | 1.1 GiB |
    | 6 | 263 s | 1.00× | 2.1% | 1.8 GiB |
    | 8 | 223 s | 1.18× | 2.2% | 2.2 GiB |
    | 10 | 202 s | 1.30× | 2.5% | 2.6 GiB |
    | 12 | 193 s | 1.36× | 3.1% | 3.0 GiB |

    - the `recompute --dry-run` at 3 workers: 649 s;

    - `--size-hints` changed no timing (193.1 s), because memory was never the limit.

    and so are the validate reports at 6 and 12 workers.
  - **Gate (deferrals review, blocker 1):** the largest count whose worst job stays within a third of its wall and CPU
    caps. At 12 the worst job used 3.1% of its CPU cap, so every count up to the CPU count passes.
  - **D-554 constants are unchanged:** retire above 512 MiB; budget 0.75 × RAM; prov-perf's charge model. The calibration
    never stressed memory. Revisit from the admission statistics the regeneration round logs for large-PROV corpora.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a fixed 10, which keeps two cores free but under-uses larger hosts;

- **D-416 (2026-10-15, pipeline-perf; user-approved 2026-10-15; reviewed by core review B: finding A (the guard now runs
  inside the try, one frame per level) and the int/dict subclass tests (B1/B2) added).** The corpus reader makes the
  same checks at a lower cost.
  - **JCS fast path:** `io.canonical.jcs_bytes` encodes a *plain* value with the stdlib `json` encoder
    (`ensure_ascii=False`, sorted keys, compact separators), which writes RFC 8785's bytes on that domain. A plain value
    is made only of exact `dict`, `list`, `str`, `int`, `bool` and `None`, with integers within ±(2⁵³−1), keys without an
    astral character (UTF-16 order is then code-point order) and depth at most 128.
  - **Fallback:** every other value, including floats, subclasses, tuples and cycles, and every error, including lone
    surrogates, goes to `rfc8785.dumps` as before. `rfc8785` stays the reference.
  - **Smaller changes:** `ingest.loaders` shares one default `IngestLimits` instead of building one per call. A register
    entry's `rid` is computed once (it was computed 5 times per entry), and its canonical bytes once per entry when the
    register is collapsed and sorted.
  - **Effect:** on agentdyn, `iter_index` 5.6–6.1 → 2.8–3.1 s and `register()` 9.3 → 2.6–2.8 s.
  - **Identity:** the same bytes everywhere. The evidence is a differential sweep of 466,848 stored documents in 8
    corpora, an exhaustive code-point test, Hypothesis differentials and scratch-import byte-diffs. None of the four
    files is in a stage code digest, so there is no regen item.
  - **Design:** `docs/reports/pipeline-perf/reader-speed-design.md`.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a compiled JCS dependency;
    - skipping canonical checks on sealed corpora;
    - caching index rows across processes;
    - replacing `rfc8785`.
